items.title: PLFR 2026 : Kiiraay défend les choix budgétaires du gouvernement
items.description: Les Cadres patriotes républicains de Kiiraay défendent les principaux choix budgétaires du gouvernement dans le cadre du projet de loi de finances rectificative (PLFR) pour l’année 2026. Dans un mémorandum consacré au texte, leur Commission Économie, Finance et Budget estime que la révision des équilibres budgétaires répond à une conjoncture économique et financière plus contraignante que prévu, tout en appelant à une programmation plus réaliste. Pour étayer cette position, Kiiraay met notamment en avant les effets des tensions au Moyen-Orient sur les marchés énergétiques, le renchérissement des coûts de financement et les perspectives de déficit pluviométrique. Ces facteurs ont conduit à revoir la croissance économique attendue en 2026 à 2,7 %, contre 5 % initialement prévus dans la loi de finances initiale. Le document souligne également le poids des subventions à l’énergie, dont l’enveloppe passe de 250 à 790,3 milliards de FCFA, soit une hausse de 540,3 milliards. Pour les auteurs du mémorandum, ce soutien vise à amortir les effets du choc énergétique sur les ménages et les entreprises, même s’il réduit les marges de manœuvre de l’État pour financer d’autres politiques publiques. Dans ce contexte, les recettes totales prévisionnelles sont ramenées de 6 188,8 à 5 848,7 milliards de FCFA, tandis que les dépenses passent de 7 433,9 à 7 583,9 milliards. Le déficit budgétaire est ainsi réévalué à 1 735,2 milliards de FCFA, contre 1 245,1 milliards initialement, soit une progression de 5,4 % à 7,6 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB). Kiiraay considère que cette rectification permet d’adapter les prévisions aux ressources mobilisables et aux nouvelles contraintes. Les auteurs relèvent toutefois des écarts importants entre les recettes attendues de certaines mesures du Plan de redressement économique et social (PRES) et les montants désormais inscrits dans le PLFR. Les recettes additionnelles associées au programme sont ainsi ramenées de 762,6 à 311,5 milliards de FCFA pour 2026. Le mémorandum aborde également la baisse des crédits d’investissement public, qui diminuent de 555 milliards de FCFA, passant de 2 803,9 à 2 248,9 milliards. Pour les cadres de Kiiraay, cette évolution appelle un suivi précis des projets concernés, afin de distinguer les révisions de crédits des éventuels reports ou abandons. Au-delà de ces ajustements, la Commission défend les orientations de redressement économique, de mobilisation des ressources nationales et de soutien au secteur productif. Elle plaide néanmoins pour davantage de transparence sur les engagements publics, une meilleure hiérarchisation des investissements et un suivi rigoureux des résultats. Le mémorandum recommande également de renforcer la traçabilité des financements et de veiller à l’apurement des arriérés de l’État envers les entreprises, notamment les PME. La position de Kiiraay consiste ainsi à soutenir le cap économique du gouvernement, tout en appelant à consolider les hypothèses budgétaires et à documenter les arbitrages opérés. Pour ses auteurs, la crédibilité de la stratégie de redressement dépendra de la capacité à traduire les engagements annoncés en résultats vérifiables.

items.title: Police hunt suspect after two people shot dead at Sakumono
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has launched a manhunt for a suspect in connection with the shooting deaths of two people at NTHC Estate, Sakumono, following an alleged financial dispute. The deceased have been identified as 57-year-old George Atuguba and his 47-year-old niece, Irene Atuguba. According to the Accra Regional Police Command, officers from the Sakumono District Police Command were dispatched to the residence on Friday, October 30, 2026, after receiving information about the incident. The officers found the bodies of the two victims lying in a pool of blood. Preliminary investigations indicate that the incident may have been triggered by a financial dispute involving George Atuguba, who had allegedly borrowed GH¢500,000 from the suspect but failed to repay the money. The suspect, identified as Samuel Christopher Osel Anto, reportedly went to the deceased’s residence on the morning of the incident with a woman identified as Beatrice Mumuni to demand repayment. A misunderstanding allegedly broke out during the encounter, leading to the suspect shooting and killing George Atuguba and his niece. The two victims were rushed to a hospital, where they were pronounced dead by a medical officer. Their bodies have since been deposited at the Police Hospital Mortuary for preservation and autopsy. The Police say efforts are underway to apprehend the suspect and bring him to justice. items.title: 2027: Rivers ADC seeks Ikwerre Elders’ support for Atiku, Amaechi
items.description: By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt The Rivers State chapter of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) has met with leaders of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality to seek support for its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and his running mate, Chibuike Rotimi Amaechi, ahead of the 2027 general elections. The party’s leadership, led by its state chairman, Dr. Chukwudi Dimkpa, visited Ogbakor Ikwerre, the apex socio-cultural organisation of the Ikwerre people, to present its candidates and solicit the elders’ support. Dimkpa told the elders and community leaders that the party considered it important to present its candidates to them as respected statesmen and custodians of Ikwerre cultural heritage. He said an Atiku-Amaechi presidency would focus on moving the country forward, adding that the ADC chose the duo because of their experience and readiness to turn around the nation’s fortunes. The state chairman also used the opportunity to formally present the party’s governorship candidate, Dr. Gabriel Pidomson, his running mate, Mr. David Okumgba, as well as its senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly candidates of Ikwerre extraction, seeking the elders’ prayers and support. “The ADC as a party recognises Ogbakor Ikwerre as a foremost socio-cultural institution representing the identity, heritage and collective interests of the Ikwerre ethnic nationality,” he said. In his address, Pidomson reminded the elders of the significance of Amaechi’s vice-presidential candidacy, describing him as an illustrious son of Ikwerre who is running alongside Atiku on the ADC presidential ticket. He expressed hope that the Atiku-Amaechi ticket would emerge victorious in the 2027 presidential election, with Atiku becoming president and Amaechi vice-president. Pidomson described the prospect of an Ikwerre son occupying the nation’s second-highest political office as significant to the political history and national participation of the ethnic nationality. He also pledged inclusive governance if elected governor of Rivers State. “If I am elected Governor of Rivers State, I promise to be a governor for all Rivers people, irrespective of ethnic background, political affiliation or other differences. “We will build a new Rivers State that will reflect the collective aspirations of its people, with emphasis on inclusive governance, unity, development and the wellbeing of citizens,” he said. In his remarks, the ADC Deputy National Chairman and Chairman of the Rivers State Governorship Campaign Council, Senator Andrew Uchendu, commended Ogbakor Ikwerre for its contributions to the development and continued existence of Rivers State. Uchendu recalled the roles played by prominent personalities, including centenarian Prof. Otonti Nduka, Chief Samson Agbaru and Prof. Augustine Ahiazu, in the struggle for greater recognition, inclusion and political representation for the Ikwerre people. He said their sacrifices and sustained efforts contributed to the emergence of three governors of Rivers State from Ikwerre extraction. The ADC delegation was received by the President-General of Ogbakor Ikwerre Cultural Organisation Worldwide, HRM King Godspower W. Onuekwa, PhD; its First Vice-President, Prof. Hilary Wordu; Prof. Otonti Nduka; Chief Samson Agbaru; Prof. Augustine Ahiazu and other prominent members. The Ogbakor Ikwerre leadership welcomed the ADC delegation and offered prayers, blessings and advice. Affaire Fallou Sène : un an de prison ferme requis contre le prévenu, délibéré fixé au 27 novembre
items.description: Huit ans après la mort de l’étudiant Fallou Sène lors d’affrontements à l’Université Gaston Berger (UGB) de Saint-Louis, le procès s’est enfin tenu devant le tribunal militaire de Dakar. À l’issue des débats, le parquet a requis un an de prison ferme contre le capitaine Serigne Moustapha Sané. Le tribunal rendra son délibéré le 27 novembre prochain. Le 15 mai 2018, une manifestation pour le paiement des bourses à l’UGB avait tourné au drame lorsqu’un escadron de gendarmerie était intervenu sur le campus. Au cours des affrontements, alors qu’un gendarme aurait été pris à partie par des manifestants, le lieutenant Moustapha Sané avait fait usage de son arme pour tenter de dégager son supérieur. Le projectile avait mortellement atteint Fallou Sène. À la barre, le capitaine Moustapha Sané, qui était sous-lieutenant au moment des faits, a reconnu être l’auteur du tir mortel. Il a expliqué avoir agi dans le cadre d’une mission officielle visant à dégager un élément pris à partie. Cet argument de défense a été réfuté par les témoignages des étudiants entendus à la barre. Le parquet a également estimé que les faits étaient constitutifs de coups et blessures volontaires ayant entraîné la mort sans intention de la donner. Le ministère public a demandé que la gravité des faits soit sanctionnée en requérant une peine d’un an de prison ferme. Mes Assane Dioma Ndiaye et Amadou Diallo ont vivement contesté la version de la défense, en pointant plusieurs irrégularités. Ils ont notamment soulevé l’illégalité de la réquisition, estimant que le recteur n’était pas l’autorité habilitée à la délivrer. Les avocats ont également dénoncé l’inadéquation de l’arme de guerre utilisée ainsi que l’absence de sanctions disciplinaires au cours de la procédure. Au titre des réparations, Me Assane Dioma Ndiaye a réclamé 200 millions de francs CFA pour la famille de Fallou Sène. Me Amadou Diallo a, pour sa part, sollicité 50 millions de francs CFA pour la Coordination des étudiants. Les avocats demandent ainsi que l’État du Sénégal assume pleinement sa responsabilité civile. De leur côté, Me Moustapha Dieng et les avocats de la défense ont contesté la constitution de partie civile des étudiants, au motif que ces derniers n’auraient pas subi de préjudice direct. Ils ont plaidé la relaxe pure et simple du capitaine Sané, invoquant l’état de nécessité, le respect des ordres et le maintien de l’ordre sur la base d’une réquisition officielle. Les avocats de la défense ont également rappelé la violence des affrontements, en produisant plus de 25 certificats médicaux attestant des blessures subies par des gendarmes. Le tribunal rendra son délibéré le 27 novembre prochain. Fatou SY

items.title: Sahara occidental : le Maroc crie victoire, le veto russe lui rappelle la réalité
items.description: Le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies a rejeté, ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026, le projet de résolution américain sur le Sahara occidental et le renouvellement du mandat de la MINURSO. La Russie a opposé son veto au texte, malgré le soutien de onze membres du Conseil. Le Pakistan, la Chine et la Somalie se sont abstenus. Revers diplomatique pour Washington et énorme déconvenue pour Rabat Ce résultat constitue un revers diplomatique pour Washington et une énorme déconvenue pour Rabat, qui espérait obtenir l'aval du Conseil de sécurité à une nouvelle orientation du processus politique. L'autodétermination, principe cardinal du droit international en matière de décolonisation, demeure au cœur du processus politique. La tentative marocaine de faire consacrer sa souveraineté sur le Sahara occidental par le Conseil de sécurité a donc échoué. Le veto russe rappelle une réalité que les célébrations marocaines tendent à occulter : aucune puissance ne peut imposer unilatéralement sa lecture du conflit au Conseil de sécurité. Le soutien américain à Rabat, aussi affirmé soit-il, ne vaut ni reconnaissance collective de souveraineté ni décision contraignante des Nations unies. Le projet américain cherchait à imprimer une nouvelle orientation forcée au processus politique en prenant des libertés avec le droit international. Mais cette orientation n'a pas obtenu le consensus nécessaire au sein de l'organe chargé du maintien de la paix et de la sécurité internationales. Un échec majeur pour Rabat Les trois abstentions méritent également attention. Celles de la Chine, du Pakistan et de la Somalie traduisent des réserves face à un texte profondément déséquilibré. Elles montrent que les interrogations sur l'équilibre du projet dépassaient la seule opposition russe. Pour Rabat, l'échec est également politique. Le Maroc pouvait espérer que l'adoption du texte consoliderait sa lecture du processus et renforcerait la place de son initiative d'autonomie dans le cadre onusien. Le statut du Sahara occidental reste une question de décolonisation non résolue. Le droit du peuple sahraoui à l'autodétermination demeure au centre du cadre juridique international. Le véto n'a pas réglé cette question. Il a empêché l'adoption d'un texte qui cherchait à réorienter de manière inéquitable le processus politique et l'avenir de la MINURSO. La portée du veto dépasse ainsi le seul échec d'un projet américain. Il rappelle que le règlement du conflit ne saurait résulter de la seule volonté de Washington ou des ambitions de Rabat. Il relève d'un processus politique conduit sous l'égide des Nations unies et respectueux du droit à l'autodétermination. L’article Sahara occidental : le Maroc crie victoire, le veto russe lui rappelle la réalité est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Intel sufre su mayor caída en Bolsa desde 1973: se hunde un 28,58% quemando 130.000 millones de dólares de capitalización
items.description: Desplome histórico de las acciones de Intel. Los títulos de la tecnológica estadounidense se han hundido este viernes un 28,58%, tras publicar unas previsiones para el cuarto trimestre por debajo de las estimaciones del mercado ante una caída de las ventas del mercado de ordenadores personales . El porcentaje significa que Intel ha firmado su peor sesión en Bolsa en 53 años. La mayor caída, hasta ahora, fue en mayo de 1973, cuando se dejó un 30%. El 2 de agosto de 2024 , se dejó un 26%, tras presentar pérdidas por el deterioro de su división de fabricación y anunciar 15.000 despidos. Con la bajada, Intel ha quemado más de 130.000 millones de dólares en capitalización bursátil, y está arrastrando a otros grupos del sector de los semiconductores como Nvidia, Broadcom, Micron Technology y AMD, que también han sufrido fuertes castigos. items.title: La FIJ lance une pétition pour la libération de Zied El-Heni
items.description: La Fédération internationale des journalistes (FIJ) a exprimé sa solidarité avec Zied El-Heni, condamné à quatre ans de prison par la chambre criminelle spécialisée dans les affaires de terrorisme du tribunal de première instance de Tunis. La FIJ, aux côtés du Syndicat national des journalistes tunisiens (SNJT), appelle les professionnels des médias et les défenseurs des droits humains à signer et relayer une pétition exigeant sa libération immédiate et inconditionnelle. «Les conditions de tenue du procès ont suscité une vive indignation. Ayant comparu à distance par visioconférence depuis la prison de la Mornaguia, le journaliste n'a pas pu assister aux plaidoiries de sa défense, ses avocats n'ayant pas été informés au préalable de son absence physique dans la salle d'audience », déplore la FIJ. Cette situation a par ailleurs été dénoncée par Zied Dabbar, président du SNJT et vice-président de la FIJ, qui pointe du doigt un procès inéquitable et une affaire montée de toutes pièces, exigeant la révision du jugement et le respect du secret des sources, rappelle la même source. De son côté, le secrétaire général de la FIJ, Anthony Bellanger, a fustigé « l'utilisation de la législation antiterroriste à des fins de répression du travail journalistique », en rappelant que la protection des sources constitue une garantie fondamentale de la liberté de la presse. items.title: Lagos warns residents of impending extreme heat
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Government has warned residents to prepare for possible extreme heat and associated environmental and public health challenges as climate outlooks indicate rising temperatures across parts of Africa, including Nigeria. The Commissioner for the Environment and Water Resources, Tokunbo Wahab, gave the advisory on Friday, urging residents to take preventive measures to protect their health and wellbeing. Wahab said the strengthening El Niño climate pattern, alongside the seasonal transition into the dry season, could contribute to unusual temperature conditions, increased heat discomfort, dry spells, dust and deteriorating air quality. He noted that although the intensity and local impact would depend on prevailing weather patterns, residents should take the emerging climate risks seriously. According to him, Lagos, as a densely populated and rapidly urbanising coastal city, could face heightened exposure to extreme heat. “The concentration of buildings, roads and other heat-absorbing infrastructure, coupled with limited green spaces and inadequate ventilation in some neighbourhoods, could intensify temperatures in built-up areas,” he said. Wahab warned that prolonged exposure to excessive heat could lead to dehydration, heat exhaustion and heatstroke, with potentially serious consequences. He identified children, older persons, pregnant women, outdoor workers, street traders, construction workers, waste handlers and people with underlying health conditions as particularly vulnerable. The commissioner urged families, employers, schools and community leaders to pay special attention to these groups and ensure that protective measures were put in place. He also cautioned that extreme heat could worsen air-quality challenges during the dry season, when dust and haze increase respiratory irritation. He added that increased reliance on petrol and diesel-powered generators during power interruptions could further worsen local air pollution. Wahab urged residents to avoid open burning of refuse and adopt environmentally responsible practices. He advised residents to drink sufficient water regularly, wear lightweight and breathable clothing, seek shade and well-ventilated spaces, and reduce strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest periods of the day. He also encouraged schools, markets, workplaces and other public facilities to provide adequate ventilation, access to drinking water and shaded areas. The commissioner urged residents to watch out for warning signs of heat-related illnesses, including excessive sweating, dizziness, headache, weakness, nausea and muscle cramps. “Anyone experiencing these symptoms should be moved to a cooler environment, given appropriate cooling assistance and taken for medical attention where necessary. “Sudden collapse or loss of consciousness should be treated as medical emergencies requiring immediate attention. “Residents with respiratory conditions are also advised to limit exposure to dusty environments and follow relevant health and air-quality advisories,” he said. Wahab stressed that preparedness must go beyond individual precautions, calling for stronger collaboration among government agencies, environmental experts, health institutions, businesses and community stakeholders. He urged residents and businesses to support efforts to reduce urban heat by protecting existing trees, promoting tree planting, preserving green spaces, ensuring proper waste disposal and discouraging environmental degradation. The commissioner said environmental sustainability and climate resilience required collective responsibility, particularly as Lagos continued to address the impacts of climate change and rapid urbanisation. He assured residents that the ministry, through its relevant agencies, would continue to engage stakeholders and promote public awareness. He added that the ministry would work with the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), Lagos State Ministry of Health and Lagos State Emergency Management Agency (LASEMA) to strengthen preparedness and response. The post Lagos warns residents of impending extreme heat appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG assures ECOWAS of peaceful 2027 elections
items.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja The Federal Government has assured the Economic Community of West African States, ECOWAS, of its commitment to conducting peaceful, credible, transparent and inclusive general elections in 2027. In a statement on Friday, the Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Bianca Odumegwu-Ojukwu, gave the assurance during a meeting with the ECOWAS Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission to Nigeria, led by former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Abuja. Odumegwu-Ojukwu said the Federal Government was committed to ensuring that the electoral process complied with the provisions of the Nigerian Constitution and relevant electoral laws. She described the 2027 general elections as a defining moment for Nigeria’s democracy, expressing optimism that the process would strengthen democratic governance in the country and the West African sub-region. The minister said institutional preparedness, transparent voter accreditation, effective management of election results and timely resolution of electoral disputes were important to building public confidence in the electoral system. She also stressed the need for effective coordination among security agencies to protect candidates, electoral officials, observers and voters before, during and after the elections. According to her, security personnel must perform their duties professionally and impartially while respecting the country’s human rights obligations. The minister further highlighted the importance of voter education and effective enforcement of electoral laws, noting that political parties, civil society organisations, traditional institutions and the media had important roles to play in ensuring peaceful elections. She expressed concern over the dangers of misinformation and disinformation, calling for accurate, accessible and timely information on the electoral process. Odumegwu-Ojukwu also identified the need to improve measures that would encourage the participation of persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups in the elections. Earlier, Foh said the mission was in Nigeria to assess the country’s preparedness for the 2027 general elections through consultations with relevant institutions and stakeholders. He said the mission had engaged the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, political parties, security agencies, civil society organisations and the media. Foh disclosed that its earlier engagements with stakeholders, including the Inter-Party Advisory Council, the Nigerian Civil Society Situation Room and the Nigerian Union of Journalists, had been constructive. He said the mission’s preliminary assessment suggested a favourable environment for the forthcoming elections, adding, however, that consultations were still ongoing. According to him, the mission would submit a report outlining its findings and recommendations at the end of the exercise. The former Sierra Leonean vice-president welcomed the assurances given by the minister and expressed optimism about Nigeria’s preparedness for the elections. He stressed the importance of sustained engagement with stakeholders and addressing identified concerns, noting that Nigeria’s ability to conduct credible elections in 2027 would have wider implications for democratic governance and stability across West Africa. The meeting ended with both sides reaffirming their commitment to promoting democracy, peace, stability and prosperity in the sub-region. The post FG assures ECOWAS of peaceful 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The State Department Is in Disarray
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. Many a heavy-handed metaphor has been constructed on the claim that Washington, D.C., is built on a swamp. This hoary cliché is also, for the most part, untrue —but the neighborhood Foggy Bottom, home to the State Department, really is former marshland . This is perhaps fitting. Stories of decadence, deviousness, and ineptitude within the current Trump administration are a dime a dozen, even at current inflation rates . The Justice Department acts as a private law firm for the president; the Department of Health and Human Services seems dedicated to undermining both; the Hegseth Pentagon is breaking globes, both physically and metaphorically . Yet the State Department has escaped some of the taint that has attached to other departments and agencies. This may be because the exploits elsewhere are so blatant, and because Secretary of State Marco Rubio has a reputation as one of the more serious figures in the administration. Whatever the reasons, the State Department may deserve more opprobrium than it has received. One of the guiding philosophies of the second Trump presidency, imported from Project 2025, is that personnel is policy: The success of an administration depends on who staffs it. State shows how this can go very wrong. Perhaps holding Kimberly Guilfoyle , the ousted ambassador to Greece who was allegedly selling access, against the department would be unfair. After all, she was a political choice, likely selected as a thank-you from the president whose campaign she assisted, and to whose son she was previously engaged. But other appointments cannot be so easily explained away. One example is Darren Beattie, whose title is senior adviser for Western Hemisphere affairs. He has particular interest in policy toward Brazil, where the administration has worked to assist the right-wing movement associated with the Bolsonaro family; he is also president of the U.S. Institute of Peace, on which Trump has scrawled his own name. Beattie’s career shows the difference between the first and second Trump administrations: When his speech to white nationalists was revealed during the first, he was fired. In the second, he was welcomed back and given a plum role. One of his colleagues now is Nate Hochman . Once seen as a rising star of mainstream conservatism, Hochman went from National Review to the 2024 presidential campaign of Ron DeSantis, from which he was fired for sharing a video featuring Nazi imagery. After a pit stop working for Senator Eric Schmitt of Missouri, who has regularly made ethnonationalist comments (yes, he’s also the guy with the Jack Smith gaffe ), he landed at the State Department, where he is reportedly Rubio’s chief speechwriter . This might explain why the secretary’s recent speech in Athens was so obsessed with supposed threats to the West. The overlapping politics does not appear to be coincidental. Jeremy Carl, who has warned that “white culture” is imperiled, missed out on a chance to join Beattie and Hochman only when his Senate hearing in February completely derailed over offensive old tweets and his inability to explain his own views. The department now has an “ Office of Remigration ,” using a white-nationalist shibboleth for ethnic cleansing. Some of the State Department’s hires are questionable less for ideological than for personality reasons. Britt McHenry, a former ESPN personality who then deployed culture-war takes to become a mid-tier MAGA figure, joined the State Department last month as a press adviser, but her time there was short: She was resigned this past Friday after throwing a drink at a fan during a Washington Wizards game. Another recent departure is Paolo Zampolli, an old Trump hanger-on most famous for introducing the president and first lady. Zampolli snagged a State Department appointment as special envoy for global partnerships, focused on cultural affairs, but then quickly began meddling in issues that were not in his remit. (Not that he was aware what his remit was: “I didn’t even read the notification” to Congress about his role. “I don’t know about the notification,” he told Politico , saying he took direction from Trump.) Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau’s attempts to control Zampolli produced what Politico described as “a monthslong fight” conducted via “emails that at times included more than a dozen administration officials.” Shortly after that scoop, Zampolli was fired . Zampolli isn’t the only one inattentive to cultural diplomacy. Officials have been rampaging against a painting in the embassy in the Dominican Republic by the artist Kehinde Wiley, who is best known (perhaps not incidentally) for painting President Obama’s official portrait. Trump officials have referred to it as “very woke,” “aesthetically terrifying,” and a lesbian picnic . (The piece is much less titillating than this might suggest: It depicts four people posing over one of Wiley’s trademark floral patterns.) Are any top officials at the State Department above this chaos? Yes, but maybe not for long. My colleague Vivian Salama reported earlier this year on the deserted halls of the department, and The Washington Sun last week reported that leaders are working to promote political loyalists but squeeze out senior foreign-service officers, the most experienced members of the nonpolitical career staff trained in foreign relations. “The State Department is trying to get people to quit,” one officer told the Sun . Sometime soon, we might get a chance to learn what happens when diplomacy is fully in the hands of the least diplomatic people imaginable. Related: The end of diplomacy Marco Rubio’s disappearing Signal chat Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Redistricting isn’t going as Republicans planned. The real threat of election interference A cynical ploy to block California’s wealth tax Today’s News An ICE officer was charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon after allegedly intentionally striking a Mexican construction worker with an SUV in Houston earlier this month. The worker, who was running away from officers, suffered a broken leg. ICE has denied that the collision was intentional, but local prosecutors say that surveillance footage contradicts the agency’s account. Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, suspended deposits and withdrawals after hackers stole an estimated $6.3 billion in digital assets , in what could be the largest crypto heist in history. The company said it would cover customers’ losses and had frozen about $3 billion in stolen assets. A crypto research firm attributed the attack to North Korean hackers. The Justice Department issued at least three dozen subpoenas and document-preservation requests in Alaska’s Senate race, as Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy launched a separate investigation into allegations that the Democrat Mary Peltola’s campaign sought to recruit a candidate with the same name as incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan to siphon votes. Peltola denied knowledge of the alleged scheme. Just Noting That Your Candy Corn Is Made of Bug Secretions By Tove Danovich Here’s a tip if you ever want to ruin a Halloween party. Seek out the most squeamish-seeming adult or child you can find in the act of consuming candy corn. Then tell them they just filled their mouth with bug secretions. If this fact alarms you—or if you’re an inveterate hater of candy corn and thus think that you have been spared—I regret to inform you that by eating many classic Halloween candies, you are, to some extent, eating bugs. items.title: Neil Zeghidour, l’entrepreneur d’origine algérienne soutenu par Nvidia qui veut « tuer » le clavier
items.description: Pour le dirigeant de Gradium, la voix pourrait progressivement s’imposer comme une interface centrale entre les humains et les machines. Fils du journaliste et éditorialiste de TV5 Monde Slimane Zeghidour, Neil Zeghidour est un chercheur français d’origine algérienne qui figure dans la liste des « 50 qui vont faire demain » de L’Obs. Son projet phare : « tuer » le clavier et le remplacer par une IA vocale. Invité du podcast de Matthieu Stefani, disponible sur YouTube depuis le 25 octobre, le cofondateur de Gradium a exposé son ambition : développer l’intelligence artificielle vocale pour rendre les interactions avec les machines plus naturelles et réduire, à terme, la place du clavier. Gradium : vers une interaction plus naturelle avec les machines L’ambition de Gradium est de permettre aux utilisateurs d’interagir avec les ordinateurs, les logiciels et les assistants personnels simplement en leur parlant. Le clavier ne disparaîtrait pas nécessairement, mais son utilisation pourrait diminuer au profit de commandes vocales. Plutôt que de naviguer entre différentes applications, l’utilisateur pourrait exprimer directement son objectif : organiser un déplacement, rechercher une information ou préparer un document. Un assistant se chargerait alors de mobiliser les outils nécessaires pour accomplir la tâche. Cette évolution est également visible dans la programmation informatique, où les développeurs peuvent désormais confier certaines missions à des agents d’IA en formulant leurs instructions en langage naturel. À terme, la multiplication de ces assistants pourrait aussi réduire le besoin de consulter constamment un écran. Des écouteurs et d’autres appareils portables pourraient ainsi devenir des points d’accès privilégiés à ces services. De Kyutai à Gradium : les origines du projet Avant de fonder Gradium, Neil Zeghidour a participé, en 2023, à la création de Kyutai, un laboratoire de recherche en intelligence artificielle à but non lucratif, avec plusieurs associés. Financé à hauteur de 300 millions d’euros par Xavier Niel, Rodolphe Saadé et Éric Schmidt, le laboratoire a notamment développé Moshi, un modèle d’intelligence artificielle vocale. Les travaux de recherche menés par l’équipe ont également contribué aux avancées du secteur de l’IA vocale et ont nourri les développements de plusieurs acteurs du domaine. Initialement, Neil Zeghidour souhaitait se consacrer à la recherche, sans ambition commerciale immédiate. Mais les sollicitations d’entreprises, notamment dans les secteurs du jeu vidéo et du smartphone, désireuses d’exploiter commercialement ces technologies ont fait émerger une nouvelle perspective. Gradium a ainsi été créé pour répondre à cette demande, avec Laurent Mazare, Olivier Teboul et Alexandre Défossez. Kyutai figure également parmi ses actionnaires. « Il y avait clairement une opportunité commerciale, mais cela sortait de la mission de Kyutai », explique Neil Zeghidour, selon Maddyness. Une IA vocale personnalisable et plus réactive Alors que plusieurs acteurs, dont OpenAI avec ChatGPT, proposent déjà des fonctionnalités vocales, Gradium entend se distinguer par la souplesse de ses modèles et la qualité de l’interaction. « Nous, on se met vraiment sur la production d’un modèle le plus agnostique possible », explique Neil Zeghidour dans le podcast de Matthieu Stefani. Le chercheur estime que les solutions existantes présentent encore des limites, notamment en matière de naturel des voix et de fluidité des échanges. Gradium entend donc fournir aux développeurs des outils leur permettant de concevoir des assistants vocaux adaptés à différents usages. « On fournit aux gens une brique pour créer des IA vocales avec n’importe quel accent, n’importe quel style, n’importe quel ton (…) On peut désigner la voix, on peut dire : “Je veux une femme de tel âge avec un accent québécois” », détaille-t-il. Cette personnalisation peut répondre à des besoins aussi bien professionnels que récréatifs. Les développeurs peuvent notamment utiliser ces technologies pour créer des assistants destinés aux standards téléphoniques ou aux jeux vidéo. La rapidité constitue un autre axe de différenciation mis en avant par le fondateur : Gradium annonce une latence de 50 millisecondes, un délai particulièrement court entre une sollicitation et la réponse du système. L’objectif est de rendre la conversation plus fluide, sans imposer à l’utilisateur le rythme artificiel d’un échange avec un logiciel. La voix, l’intonation et la réactivité participent ainsi à l’expérience proposée. Selon une publication LinkedIn de Matthieu Stefani, qui a interviewé le chercheur, les modèles de Gradium couvrent plusieurs fonctions : la transcription, la synthèse vocale et la traduction en temps réel. NVIDIA rejoint les investisseurs de Gradium Dans un communiqué publié sur son site le 8 juillet 2026, Gradium a annoncé avoir porté son financement à plus de 100 millions de dollars, avec l’arrivée de nouveaux investisseurs, dont le géant américain des puces électroniques et de l’IA NVIDIA. Cette annonce fait suite à une première levée de fonds de 60 millions de dollars au lancement de l’entreprise. « Dépasser 100 millions de dollars de financement et développer nos investisseurs marque une étape importante pour Gradium. Cela nous permet d’accélérer notre feuille de route, d’étendre notre présence dans la région de la baie de San Francisco et d’apporter des années de recherche révolutionnaire sur les produits utilisés par les développeurs et les entreprises du monde entier », indique l’entreprise. L’incontournable de l’IA étend sa présence dans la Silicon Valley. L’article Neil Zeghidour, l'entrepreneur d'origine algérienne soutenu par Nvidia qui veut « tuer » le clavier est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Cyberbullying : Okafor’s lawyer faults Sowore, others over sentimental support for Ogala
items.description: By Henry Ojelu Counsel to Pastor Chris Okafor, Mr Ife Ajayi, has faulted the sentimental support for Nollywood actress Doris Ogala over her cyberbullying trial, insisting that freedom of expression does not confer the right to make false and malicious allegations against others without regard for the law. Ajayi, who spoke in an interview with Vanguard, was reacting to comments by activist Omoyele Sowore and Ogala over alleged injustice in the ongoing trial. He argued that the right to freedom of expression was not absolute and must be exercised within the limits prescribed by law, particularly where allegations, blackmail and extortion were involved. According to him, the issues leading to the criminal proceedings should not be treated as a mere disagreement between individuals, but viewed against the background of alleged violations of the rights of others. Ajayi advised the public to obtain copies of the charges proffered against her. He described her unlawful conduct as a deliberate act that violated the rights of his client and was capable of inciting the public against an individual. He also urged members of the public to exercise caution in endorsing false allegations made by the actress, insisting that such claims should be subjected to legal scrutiny rather than public sentiment. Expressing confidence in the judiciary, the lawyer said he was optimistic that the court would deliver justice based on the overwhelming print, audio and video evidence in compliance with the applicable laws. “I am 100 per cent optimistic that the court will do what is right. The court, in all fairness, even after the defendant’s lawyer pleaded with it to release her on bail and offered to take responsibility for her conduct, gave the prosecution 48 hours to respond,” he said. Ajayi also faulted Ogala’s conduct during the court proceedings, alleging that her outburst and disruption of proceedings raised questions about her ability to abide by the conditions of her release. He said the incident suggested that even her counsel might have difficulty guaranteeing her conduct if she were granted bail. The lawyer maintained that the courtroom was not a place for emotional outbursts or disrespect, stressing that parties to a legal proceeding were expected to conduct themselves in accordance with established rules. “You cannot behave disrespectfully at a police station or anywhere else and expect to do the same in a court of law. The court is where logic and legal accountability prevail,” he said. Ajayi further called on the National Assembly to consider stricter legislation against the practice of publicly calling out individuals over private disagreements, particularly where such actions could damage reputations or violate the rights of others. He argued that personal grievances should be addressed through appropriate legal channels rather than through public accusations and campaigns. “The law is not about emotion or sentiment. It is about logic and legal accountability. It is a place where people are held accountable for their unlawful conduct,” he said. He urged members of the public not to accept allegations made in the course of the dispute as established facts, stressing that the court remained the appropriate institution to determine the issues before it. The post Cyberbullying : Okafor’s lawyer faults Sowore, others over sentimental support for Ogala appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Make Me Stay: Joy Prime’s exciting new dating show premieres Nov. 1
items.description: Can 60 seconds spark a lasting connection? Joy Prime ’s new dating reality show, Make Me Stay , is set to put first impressions, attraction and the search for love to the ultimate test when it premieres on November 1, 2026. Finding love can be unpredictable, but what happens when you have just 60 seconds to make someone interested in you? Designed to bring excitement, spontaneity and entertainment to the dating experience, Make Me Stay explores the power of first impressions and the possibility of finding a meaningful connection in an unexpected moment. The show brings together singles looking for love and gives them an opportunity to introduce themselves, express their personalities and make a memorable impression. With just one minute to capture someone’s interest, participants must find creative ways to stand out and convince a potential match that they are worth getting to know. But beyond the fun, excitement and pressure of the 60-second encounters lies a bigger question: Can genuine attraction develop from a brief first meeting? Make Me Stay promises viewers an entertaining look at modern dating, exploring attraction, confidence, communication and the different things people look for when choosing a potential partner. From unexpected connections to interesting personalities and unpredictable moments, the show is set to offer viewers a refreshing perspective on the search for love. As dating continues to evolve, Make Me Stay brings the conversation to television, challenging singles to step out of their comfort zones and discover whether one minute could be the beginning of something special. With its premiere scheduled for November 1, 2026 at 8 P.M., viewers can look forward to a new dating experience filled with excitement, chemistry and the possibility of love. Tune in to Joy Prime from 1st November and be part of the journey.

items.title: Sahara : Washington rappelle l’échec du référendum et défend une autre voie pour l’autodétermination
items.description: Lors de la séance du Conseil de sécurité consacrée au Sahara, ce vendredi 30 octobre, le représentant des États-Unis a estimé que l’impossibilité d’organiser un référendum avait été reconnue par les Nations unies depuis plusieurs décennies. Pour étayer sa position, le diplomate américain a rappelé les mises en garde de plusieurs anciens secrétaires généraux de l’ONU et responsables de la MINURSO, tout en affirmant que le droit à l’autodétermination ne se limite pas nécessairement à l’organisation d’un référendum. La question du référendum au Sahara a occupé une place centrale dans l’intervention du représentant américain au Conseil de sécurité. Dans le contexte des discussions autour du renouvellement du mandat de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO), le diplomate a défendu une réorientation des missions de la force onusienne en fonction de l’évolution du processus politique. Cette séance a également été marquée par une confrontation diplomatique entre Washington et Moscou. La Russie a en effet opposé son veto au projet de résolution américain portant sur le renouvellement du mandat de la MINURSO et la réorientation de ses missions. Dans son intervention, le représentant des États-Unis a remis en question la faisabilité de l’organisation d’un référendum, en s’appuyant sur plusieurs prises de position de responsables onusiens au cours des trente dernières années. Selon lui, les difficultés rencontrées depuis les années 1990 montrent que cette option ne correspond plus aux réalités du processus politique. Russia just vetoed a U.S. resolution, backed by 11 Security Council members, that would have taken historic steps toward ending the 50-year Western Sahara conflict. We must not fall back on a status quo that condemns refugees to another five decades in the camps—especially when… pic.twitter.com/LZk2rBfYvi — Ambassador Mike Waltz (@USAmbUN) October 30, 2026 Washington s'appuie sur les positions d'anciens responsables de l'ONU Pour étayer son argumentaire, le diplomate américain est notamment revenu sur les déclarations de l’ancien secrétaire général des Nations unies, Boutros Boutros-Ghali. Celui-ci ne prévoyait déjà pas la tenue du référendum en 1996, alors que le Conseil de sécurité avait été contraint de suspendre le processus en raison des désaccords sur l’identification des personnes habilitées à participer au vote. Le représentant américain a également évoqué la période de Kofi Annan à la tête de l’ONU. En 1997, ce dernier avait mis en garde contre l’impossibilité de tenir le référendum à la date prévue de 1999. Les réserves se sont ensuite accentuées au fil des années. Selon le diplomate, Kofi Annan et son envoyé personnel de l’époque, James Baker, avaient fini par considérer que la mise en œuvre du plan de règlement était devenue peu probable. Ils avaient également soumis au Conseil de sécurité la possibilité de mettre entièrement fin à la mission de la MINURSO. L'intervention américaine a aussi rappelé un avertissement formulé par Kofi Annan en 2003 : même si le référendum venait à être organisé, le Conseil de sécurité ne serait pas nécessairement en mesure d'en faire appliquer les résultats. Le représentant de Washington a enfin cité les propos d'un ancien responsable de la direction de la MINURSO, qui avait estimé en 2005 que le plan référendaire adopté par le Conseil de sécurité avait échoué et que ses chances de mise en œuvre étaient désormais inexistantes. Le droit à l’autodétermination au-delà du référendum Pour le diplomate américain, ces différents éléments ne constituent pas une nouvelle lecture imposée par Washington, mais renvoient à des constats formulés par des responsables des Nations unies eux-mêmes au cours de trois décennies. Il a ainsi estimé que le maintien de la référence au référendum dans les discussions sur l’avenir de la MINURSO, y compris au prix d’un veto au Conseil de sécurité, ne change rien au fait que l’ONU n’a pas réussi à organiser cette consultation depuis plusieurs décennies. Le représentant américain a toutefois tenu à préciser que son pays ne renonçait pas au principe de l’autodétermination. Il a soutenu que ce droit et l’expression de la volonté des peuples ne passent pas nécessairement par un référendum et peuvent également prendre d’autres formes politiques. The post Sahara : Washington rappelle l’échec du référendum et défend une autre voie pour l’autodétermination appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : un sommet sur le sport et le développement durable s’ouvre ce samedi à Dakar
items.description: Un sommet consacré au « Sport et développement durable » se tient ce samedi 31 octobre 2026 à Dakar, autour des enjeux de financement du sport, de valorisation de l’héritage des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) et de promotion de la performance africaine. Selon le programme de la rencontre, les échanges porteront notamment sur les mécanismes de financement et le développement durable du sport, ainsi que sur les moyens de transformer l’élan suscité par les JOJ en opportunités durables. La rencontre accordera également une place à la jeunesse, à travers une séquence intitulée « Notre avenir, nos questions », et au partage d’expériences sur le parcours des sportifs africains, du talent au podium. Le sommet abordera aussi la place du sport dans la vision de développement du Sénégal, avec une séquence consacrée à la vision présidentielle, suivie d’échanges autour de la vision sportive des États et d’une séquence réunissant des chefs d’État. Prévue de 8 heures à 13 h 30, la rencontre s’achèvera par une séance de conclusion, suivie d’un déjeuner et d’un moment de réseautage. Selon la même source, cette initiative s’inscrit dans une réflexion sur le rôle du sport comme levier de développement durable et sur les perspectives à construire autour de l’héritage des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse.

items.title: Police arrest 40-year-old man with 91 parcels of suspected Indian hemp at Circle
items.description: The Ghana Police Service has arrested a 40-year-old man, Roger Borbobli, after allegedly finding 91 parcels of substances suspected to be Indian hemp in his possession at the VIP Bus Terminal at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra. The arrest was made on October 29, 2026, by officers from the Office of the Special Operations Assistant to the Inspector-General of Police (IGP), following information that the suspect had been spotted at the terminal with three suitcases containing the suspected narcotics. According to preliminary investigations, some loading boys at the terminal detected an unusual smell coming from the suitcases and alerted the Police. A team of officers subsequently arrived at the scene, arrested the suspect and retrieved the three suitcases, which contained 91 parcels of compressed dried leaves suspected to be Indian hemp. The suspect reportedly valued the seized substances at GH¢33,600. During interrogation, Mr Borbobli allegedly told investigators that he was a farmer from Sovie Kudzra, near Kpando in the Volta North Region. He reportedly admitted cultivating Indian hemp but said the parcels found in his possession had been acquired from another farmer, identified as Benjamin, from the same community. The exhibits are expected to be forwarded to the Police Forensic Crime Laboratory for analytical examination. The suspect remains in Police custody, assisting investigations, and is expected to be brought before the court to face justice.

items.title: ‎NSITF seeks stronger enforcement of Employees’ Compensation Act to protect workers’ rights
items.description: ‎ ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎ ‎ABUJA — MANAGING Director and Chief Executive of the Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), Mr. Oluwaseun Faleye, has urged the judiciary to strengthen the interpretation, adjudication, and enforcement of the Employees’ Compensation Act (ECA) 2010, so that Nigerian workers can fully enjoy the justice and protection the law guarantees. ‎ ‎The Act provides compensation for employees—or their dependants—who suffer death, injury, disability, or occupational disease arising from employment. ‎ ‎Faleye, in his welcome address at the opening of the NSITF 2026 Legal Stakeholders’ Engagement in Abuja, ‎emphasised that legislation alone is not enough; workers need timely dispute resolution, fair hearings, and effective compliance with court orders to turn statutory rights into real benefits. ‎The theme of the two-day event is “Enhancing Judicial Interpretation, Adjudication and Enforcement under the Employees’ Compensation Act (ECA), 2010.” ‎ ‎Mr. Faleye noted that while last year’s engagement focused on strengthening collaboration for the sustainable administration of the Employees’ Compensation Scheme, this year’s edition addresses a deeper question: how statutory rights can be translated into practical justice. ‎ ‎Drawing on the experience of everyday Nigerian workers — mothers, construction workers, factory employees and drivers who leave home each day expecting to return he observed that a workplace accident instantly becomes a human crisis with financial, emotional and social consequences. ‎ ‎”Does the law provide a framework for protection? Yes. Does the Employees’ Compensation Act establish a system for compensation for work-related injury, disease, disability or death? Yes. But the existence of a law does not by itself guarantee that its promise will be fulfilled,” Mr. Faleye said. ‎ ‎He explained that the effectiveness of the ECA depends on three interconnected stages — interpretation, adjudication and enforcement: ‎”First, are the provisions being understood and applied in a manner consistent with their wording, purpose and legal context? ‎ ‎”Second, are disputes being resolved fairly, on evidence and applicable law, without avoidable delay? Third, are lawful decisions and orders being given effect so that justice does not end with the pronouncement of judgment? Weakness at any stage can undermine confidence in the entire system.” ‎ ‎The NSITF Managing Director underscored the pivotal role of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria (NICN) in labour justice, noting that the Court’s interpretation of the Employees’ Compensation Act has consequences beyond the immediate parties to a dispute. ‎ ‎Such decisions, he said, clarify rights, guide the conduct of employers and employees, and shape the resolution of future disputes. ‎ ‎For workers, he said, justice means the practical realisation of their entitlements; for employers, it means a predictable legal environment. The credibility of the Scheme, he added, rests on workers’ confidence that legitimate claims will be addressed and on employers’ confidence that their obligations will be determined fairly. ‎ ‎Mr. Faleye, a legal practitioner, affirmed that the Fund will continue to strengthen its administrative processes, improve claims handling, promote awareness and encourage employer compliance. He acknowledged, however, that the NSITF cannot achieve these objectives in isolation. ‎ ‎He urged participants to treat the engagement not as a ceremonial gathering, but as an opportunity to identify practical solutions, highlight areas requiring greater legal clarity, improve cooperation, reduce avoidable disputes and promote compliance. ‎ ‎”The value of a stakeholder engagement lies not merely in the quality of speeches delivered but in the clarity of understanding it produces and the improvements that follow,” he said, calling for frank, informed and constructive deliberations that will yield actionable recommendations for strengthening the administration of the Scheme. ‎ ‎”May our deliberations strengthen the rule of law and ensure that the promise of protection becomes a reality for Nigerian workers,” he added. ‎ ‎In his goodwill message, the Honourable Minister of Labour and Employment, Alhaji Muhammadu Maigari Dingyadi, stated that the strength of a nation lies not merely in the laws it makes, but in the wisdom with which those laws are applied and the integrity of the institutions entrusted with their administration. ‎ ‎While laws may establish rights and define obligations, the Minister said, public confidence ultimately rests on the assurance that justice will be administered fairly, impartially and with due regard for the dignity of every individual. ‎ ‎Recalling the enduring words of the late Justice Chukwudifu Oputa that “the judiciary is the last hope of the common man,” the Minister observed that “…this statement carries a profound responsibility. ‎ ‎It reminds us that for many citizens, the justice system represents their final recourse when other avenues have failed. Such trust must never be taken lightly.” Such trust, he said, demands wisdom in judgment, integrity in public service and an unwavering commitment to fairness. ‎ ‎The Minister reaffirmed the Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment’s belief that a just and productive society must be built on respect for the law, responsible institutions and a shared commitment to the public good, and urged all stakeholders in the administration of the ECA to approach their responsibilities with these values in mind. ‎ ‎”The credibility of our institutions is strengthened not by words alone, but by the quality and integrity of their actions,” he stressed. ‎ ‎He commended the NSITF Management under Mr. Faleye for convening the engagement, describing it as an important national initiative aimed at strengthening the implementation of the ECA 2010. ‎ ‎ He also expressed appreciation to the President of the National Industrial Court, distinguished members of the Bench and Bar, and all participants for their commitment. ‎ ‎”May your deliberations be guided by wisdom, enriched by experience and directed towards outcomes that strengthen public confidence in our institutions,” the Minister said. ‎ ‎Delivering the keynote address, the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria, Hon. Justice Benedict Bakwaph Kanyip, advocated institutional synergy to strengthen the Employees’ Compensation Scheme and ensure that its benefits reach the intended beneficiaries. ‎ ‎He commended the NSITF for creating a platform that will enhance the Scheme in the overall interest of Nigerians and the workplace, adding that robust engagement with the judiciary will further boost the Fund’s impact on service delivery under the Scheme. ‎ ‎The event drew senior government and judicial officials, including the President of the National Industrial Court of Nigeria; the Permanent Secretary, Federal Ministry of Labour and Employment; Honourable Justices of the National Industrial Court; members of the Bench and Bar; Employers’ Associations; organised labour; and development partners. The post ‎NSITF seeks stronger enforcement of Employees’ Compensation Act to protect workers’ rights appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La France hausse le ton contre Moscou après son veto sur le Sahara et réaffirme sa position en faveur du Maroc
items.description: La France a vivement regretté le vote contre la résolution du Conseil de sécurité de la part de la Russie sur le Sahara, vendredi soir. « Il est temps d'avancer, le statu quo n'est pas une option » , a tancé la délégation française en s'adressant à Moscou. Vendredi soir, la Russie a opposé son droit de veto au Conseil de sécurité face à une résolution ambitieuse qui devait permettre d'avancer dans le règlement politique du dossier du Sahara. Intervenant à l'issue du vote russe, la délégation française n'a pas mâché ses mots pour exprimer sa désapprobation de la position russe, en mettant en garde contre les conséquences d'une fermeture de la mission dans un contexte de tensions régionales. La France a regretté le rejet par la Russie du projet de résolution américain visant à renouveler le mandat de la Mission des Nations unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum au Sahara occidental (MINURSO) et tenu également à réitérer sa position sur le dossier du Sahara. « Pour la France, le présent et l'avenir du Sahara occidental s'inscrivent dans le cadre de la souveraineté marocaine. C'est donc bien sur la seule base du plan d'autonomie marocain que nous appelons au réengagement des discussions pour aboutir à une solution juste, durable et négociée » , a déclaré le chef de délégation française au Conseil de sécurité. Le projet de résolution présenté par les États-Unis, a poursuivi la délégation française, représentait un important pas en avant en faveur du processus politique. Rappelant que la résolution 2797 adoptée l'année dernière avait marqué un tournant décisif pour le règlement définitif du conflit, Paris a soutenu: « Il est navrant que le Conseil ne soit pas en mesure de construire sur ses acquis ». « Il est impératif que les discussions reprennent en vue d'une solution négociée, juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable », a ajouté la France, soulignant que la Minurso joue un rôle essentiel pour la stabilité de la région et « aide à favoriser la confiance que requiert l'avancement du processus politique ». « Sa fermeture abrupte serait extrêmement préoccupante dans un contexte de regain des tensions dans la zone », a estimé Paris. « Nous déplorons le rejet de cette résolution par des membres du Conseil alors qu'elle exprimait le soutien de ce Conseil au Commissariat aux réfugiés pour la mise en place de solutions durables pour les réfugiés sahraouis dans le plein respect du droit des réfugiés », a conclu la délégation française en soulignant qu' « il est temps d'avancer, le statu quo n'est pas une option ». items.title: ₦70,000 transport allowance: Federal pensioners decry exclusion, unpaid ₦25,000 palliative
items.description: — Beg Tinubu to intervene By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — CONTROVERSY over the recent approval of ₦70,000 for Federal Government workers has continued unabated, as the Federal Parastatals and Private Sector Pensioners Association of Nigeria (FEPPPAN) has appealed to President Bola Tinubu to extend the newly approved ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance for public servants to pensioners. The retired government workers lamented that retirees were being left behind in government efforts to cushion the effects of rising living costs. FEPPPAN said pensioners also pay transportation fares to hospitals for medical care, markets to purchase essential commodities, and other destinations for economic activities they undertake to supplement their pensions and sustain their livelihoods. In a statement jointly signed by its President-General, Elder Benjamin Maisamari Amako, and General Secretary, Mr Franklin Erinle, the association questioned why retirees should be excluded from transportation support when they equally bear the burden of rising fares and other costs of living. According to the statement: “The association questioned the rationale behind excluding pensioners from transportation support when they equally bear the burden of rising transport fares and other costs of living. “FEPPPAN expressed further disappointment over the continued non-payment of the ₦25,000 monthly subsidy-removal palliative announced by the Federal Government in October 2023, lamenting that eligible pensioners were still awaiting the promised relief even as another support package had been approved for serving workers.” It called for immediate presidential intervention to address the concerns of pensioners. The statement said: “FEPPPAN expresses concern that eligible pensioners are yet to receive the promised support, describing the continued wait as a source of frustration for retirees who had hoped that the intervention would provide some relief from the prevailing economic hardship. “Against this background, the association called on President Tinubu to urgently intervene by directing the relevant government agencies to ensure the payment of the outstanding ₦25,000 subsidy-removal palliative to eligible pensioners. “It also urged the President to ensure that pensioners are included in the new ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance arrangement, stressing that retirees should not be left out of policies intended to protect Nigerians from the effects of rising living costs.” It clarified that its appeal was not against the transport allowance approved for serving workers, but against the apparent neglect of retirees in the government’s response to the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It lamented that pensioners, many of whom depend on fixed monthly incomes to pay for food, medication, transportation and other necessities, were being left to contend with rising expenses without comparable relief. FEPPPAN recalled that on October 1, 2023, the Federal Government announced a ₦25,000 monthly palliative for three months to cushion the effects of petrol subsidy removal, with vulnerable pensioners among the groups identified for assistance. It said the continued wait for the promised relief had deepened retirees’ frustration and hardship. The association urged Tinubu to direct the relevant government agencies to expedite the payment of the outstanding palliative to eligible pensioners and ensure their inclusion in the new ₦70,000 monthly transport allowance arrangement. FEPPPAN maintained that pensioners deserved the same consideration in government policies intended to ease economic hardship, stressing that their years of service to the country should not leave them forgotten when relief measures are being implemented. items.title: IGP secures Italian training offer for 5,000 police officers
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, has secured an offer of specialised training for up to 5,000 Nigeria Police Force personnel in Italy as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s response to terrorism and other security threats. The proposed training, focusing on counter-insurgency operations and policing in difficult rural and forested terrains, followed Disu’s working visit to Italy, where he held discussions with Italian law enforcement authorities on security cooperation, technology transfer and institutional development. The initiative is aimed at enhancing the operational capacity of the police to tackle terrorism, kidnapping, arms trafficking and other criminal activities through intelligence-led policing and improved tactical capabilities. A statement issued on Friday by the Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, said the proposed training would cover tactical operations, intelligence-led patrols, protection of critical infrastructure, digital and scientific forensics, cybercrime, explosives detection, financial investigations, asset tracing and anti-extortion techniques. It said the programme would extend beyond the Police Mobile Force to include specialised units such as explosive ordnance disposal and forensic teams. During the visit, Disu met with the Commander General of the Italian Carabinieri, Lieutenant-General Salvatore Luongo, to explore opportunities for technical assistance, specialised training and institutional cooperation. The IGP and his delegation also visited the Carabinieri Centre of Excellence for Stability Police Units (CoESPU) in Vicenza, where they assessed training facilities and explored ways of adapting specialised programmes to Nigeria’s security challenges. Among the proposals discussed were command courses for 40 senior police officers, leadership training for 100 junior commanders and the deployment of a mobile assistance team to support Police Mobile Force training schools in Gwoza and Ila-Orangun. The delegation also sought Italian support for developing a national stability policing doctrine and standard operating procedures to promote professionalism, operational consistency and civilian protection, particularly in communities recovering from conflict. Further discussions focused on possible cooperation in canine operations, forensic science and mounted policing, including horse breeding and local capacity development for public order management and other policing responsibilities. To facilitate the implementation of the proposed initiatives, Disu proposed a memorandum of understanding covering training, technology transfer and operational doctrine. He also invited an assessment team from the Italian Carabinieri to Abuja to identify priority areas and develop practical implementation strategies. The Inspector-General reaffirmed the commitment of the Nigeria Police Force to international partnerships aimed at strengthening operational readiness, improving investigative capacity and enhancing the protection of lives and property. The Force said it would continue engaging relevant international partners to advance the proposals in line with Nigeria’s security priorities and efforts to build a more professional, capable and responsive police institution.
