items.title: ‘Debt Worse Than Leprosy’: Obasanjo tackles Tinubu
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta Former President Olusegun Obasanjo has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s defence of government borrowing, declaring that debt is worse than leprosy because of its devastating consequences for present and future generations. Obasanjo also warned Nigeria and other African countries against allowing foreign interests to dominate artificial intelligence, AI, saying the emerging technology could become another instrument of exploitation and digital colonialism if the continent failed to develop its own technological capacity. The former president spoke on Friday in Abeokuta, Ogun State, at the Ajibosin Platform, a public forum themed, “Leveraging Artificial Intelligence to Solve Grassroots Problems and Accelerate National Development”. Reacting to Tinubu’s earlier assertion that borrowing was not leprosy, Obasanjo argued that the accumulation of public debt could mortgage the country’s future and impose an unbearable burden on generations yet unborn. “And for anybody to say debt is no leprosy, is absolute nonsense. Debt is worse than leprosy because leprosy destroys only one person. Debt destroys generations,” he declared. Tinubu had defended his administration’s borrowing policy in April, insisting that borrowing was not inherently wrong if the country had the capacity to repay. “If we have to borrow, we borrow. Borrowing is not leprosy; we just have to work hard to be able to pay for it,” the President had said during a meeting with Plateau State leaders, led by Governor Caleb Mutfwang and the National Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, at the State House. The President’s position came amid concerns over Nigeria’s rising debt profile and the increasing proportion of government revenue committed to debt servicing. Obasanjo also questioned Nigeria’s economic performance over the years, particularly the depreciation of the naira against the United States dollar. Recounting his experience as a farmer, he said the naira was stronger than the dollar when he established his farm 47 years ago. “When I started my farm, 47 years ago, naira to the dollar was one naira to $1.85. Forty-seven years ago. What has Nigeria done in 47 years that we now have 1,500 naira to a dollar? What have we done?” he asked. He challenged the country’s political leadership to demonstrate its understanding of Nigeria’s problems and identify practical solutions to the challenges confronting the nation. “What do our leaders know? And what do they not know? And from what they know, what can they do for us?” he queried. The former president also faulted Nigeria’s dependence on the World Bank and International Monetary Fund (IMF), arguing that their economic prescriptions were not necessarily designed to address the country’s peculiar circumstances. “World Bank and IMF were not designed for us. They were not built by us. They were built before we became independent. And that’s the people who would determine what we do,” he said. He urged Nigerian leaders to scrutinise foreign economic prescriptions and ensure that national policies reflected the country’s interests and development priorities. Turning to artificial intelligence, Obasanjo warned that Africa risked repeating the mistakes of its colonial past if it allowed foreign interests to control the technology and its applications. Although he acknowledged that he was not technically knowledgeable about AI, he said ownership and control were critical to ensuring that the technology served African interests. “I don’t know too much technically about AI, but I know that anything that is not under your control can be abused against you. And you can see that this has already started,” he said. Drawing parallels between AI and Africa’s historical experiences with slavery, colonialism and economic dependency, Obasanjo urged African leaders to approach the technological revolution with caution. He also questioned the concept of technology transfer, asking African countries to examine the terms and benefits of their engagements with foreign technology providers. “But what exactly is technology transfer? Who transferred technology to them, and what did they pay for it?” he queried. Obasanjo further criticised what he described as unequal international economic arrangements, citing restrictions on agricultural subsidies for developing countries despite continued support for farmers in developed economies. He expressed concern over the estimated 24 million Nigerian children out of school, warning that the situation could create serious challenges for future generations. “We have 24 million Nigerian children who should be in school but are not. If you are looking for the disasters of tomorrow, these children represent one of them,” he said. He challenged policymakers and technology stakeholders to explore how AI could improve access to education and address learning challenges. On agriculture, Obasanjo advocated the deployment of artificial intelligence to help farmers identify suitable crops, improve productivity and strengthen food and nutrition security. Also speaking at the event, guest speaker and historian, Dr Umar Ardo, warned that Africa could be entering another phase of economic exploitation through artificial intelligence if it failed to secure ownership and control of its data, technological infrastructure and intellectual resources. In a presentation titled, “From Slave Ships to Server Farms: Artificial Intelligence and Africa’s Unbroken History of Extraction”, Ardo argued that although AI offered significant opportunities for economic transformation, it could deepen existing inequalities if African countries remained dependent on foreign technology companies. He said the continent must move beyond adopting foreign innovations and address fundamental questions surrounding ownership, control, regulation and the distribution of economic benefits. “AI offers Africa important opportunities, but without ownership, safeguards and public purpose, it could extend a long history in which Africa supplies value while others control and capture it,” he said. Tracing Africa’s economic history over five centuries, Ardo identified the transatlantic slave trade, colonial exploitation of natural resources and post-independence economic dependency as major phases of external extraction. He explained that while the slave trade commodified African lives, colonialism focused largely on exploiting mineral and agricultural resources, while many post-independence economies remained dependent on exporting raw materials and importing finished products. According to him, infrastructure and technologies introduced during colonial rule, including railways, steam engines and administrative systems, were largely organised around extracting African resources and transporting them to foreign markets. “We supplied resources and labour; others controlled the machinery and captured much of the value,” he stated. Ardo also identified the migration of highly trained African professionals, including doctors, nurses, engineers and scientists, to foreign countries as another dimension of the continent’s continuing resource losses. He warned that data could become the next major commodity in Africa’s history of external extraction, noting that information generated by citizens, hospitals, farmers, businesses, indigenous communities and public institutions was increasingly valuable to the global digital economy. “Data may become the fourth commodity in this long history of extraction,” he cautioned. The historian expressed concern that the infrastructure for processing information, developing AI models and generating intellectual property and commercial profits remained disproportionately controlled outside Africa. He questioned who benefited when farmers’ agricultural practices, patients’ medical records, indigenous languages, traditional medicine and cultural knowledge were incorporated into AI systems developed by foreign companies. “When farmers’ planting patterns are recorded, who controls that knowledge; the farmer or the platform?” he asked. Ardo canvasses local AI development, data sovereignty To prevent artificial intelligence from becoming another instrument of economic dependency, Ardo proposed a framework anchored on technological sovereignty, data protection, indigenous innovation, grassroots development and continental cooperation. He called for stronger legal and institutional safeguards against the uncontrolled exploitation of personal data and traditional knowledge. While acknowledging the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 as an important step towards protecting citizens’ information, he said privacy protection alone was insufficient to guarantee data sovereignty. He advocated additional mechanisms to protect community knowledge, ensure fair compensation and guarantee Africans a reasonable share of the commercial value generated from their data and intellectual resources. Ardo urged the Federal Government to increase investment in domestic computing capacity, reliable energy infrastructure, semiconductor technology, research institutions and indigenous AI development. He maintained that Nigeria, with a population exceeding 230 million, should not remain merely a consumer market for foreign technology. “A country of over 230 million people should be more than a market for foreign technology,” he declared. He also called for the development of locally controlled datasets and AI models capable of understanding African languages, agricultural practices, medicinal traditions and customary knowledge under African ownership and appropriate safeguards. On grassroots development, Ardo urged governments to ensure that communities benefited directly from AI applications in primary healthcare, agricultural extension services, local government administration, revenue collection, conflict resolution and disaster management. He further advocated comprehensive AI training programmes in universities, polytechnics and colleges of education to develop software developers, technicians, data stewards and other professionals. On continental cooperation, he urged Nigeria to work with other African countries to harmonise data governance regulations, develop shared technological infrastructure and strengthen the continent’s bargaining power in engagements with international technology companies. He identified the African Union’s Data Policy Framework, adopted in 2022, as an important foundation for coordinated continental action. Warning that digital extraction could be more difficult to identify and resist than the exploitation of physical resources, Ardo said information could cross national borders without the knowledge or meaningful understanding of the people and communities generating it. “One of the most efficient systems of extraction is the one its subjects volunteer to use,” he warned. He urged African leaders to approach the AI revolution with a clear understanding of the continent’s history, insisting that Africa must become a builder, owner and rule-maker in the global technology ecosystem rather than remain a passive consumer of foreign innovations. Drawing a comparison between Africa’s historical experiences and the emerging digital economy, he said: “Five centuries ago, they came for our bodies. Then they came for our land and its riches. Then our commodities and trained minds. Today, they come for our data.” He, however, maintained that Africa still had the opportunity to determine its technological future. “The choice is ours. Artificial intelligence can become another instrument through which Africa is managed, or an instrument through which Africa begins to manage its own destiny,” he added. items.title: Sanwo-Olu urges Lagosians to trust Hamzat, avoid experiment
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has urged residents to support his deputy, Dr Obafemi Hamzat, describing him as an experienced administrator capable of sustaining the state’s development if elected governor in 2027. Sanwo-Olu made the appeal on Friday at the official unveiling of Hamzat’s seven-pillar development manifesto, tagged PROMISE, at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts, formerly the National Theatre, Iganmu, Lagos. The governor cautioned residents against experimenting with the state’s leadership, insisting that Lagos required continuity to consolidate its development gains. The event attracted former Governor Babatunde Fashola, members of the Lagos State Executive Council, party chieftains, religious leaders, traditional rulers, media executives, local government chairmen, captains of industry and other dignitaries. Speaking as Special Guest of Honour, Sanwo-Olu described Hamzat, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate, as a dependable partner who had demonstrated commitment to the state’s development throughout their seven years in office. Using a relay race as an analogy for political succession, he said Lagos needed an experienced successor who understood the administration’s policies and ongoing projects. Recalling the political developments of September 2018, Sanwo-Olu said Hamzat had stepped aside from his governorship ambition following appeals by party leaders and agreed to become his running mate. “In seven years, there has not been one day—not one—when I had to wonder whose side my deputy was on. “Governors and their deputies have torn states apart in this country. In Lagos, there has been one government, one direction, and one voice,” he said. Sanwo-Olu cited Hamzat’s involvement in critical government decisions, including the management of the COVID-19 pandemic, the October 2020 unrest and the execution of major infrastructure projects such as the Blue and Red rail lines and the Lekki Deep Sea Port. He also traced Hamzat’s public service career to 2005, when he served as Commissioner for Science and Technology under the administration of former Governor Bola Tinubu. He subsequently served as Commissioner for Works and Infrastructure under Fashola, during which he was involved in major infrastructure projects, including the Lekki-Ikoyi Link Bridge, before becoming deputy governor in 2019. The governor said Hamzat’s experience across three successive administrations had equipped him with an understanding of the state’s governance structure and development priorities. On the transition of power, Sanwo-Olu described a peaceful succession as one of the most important legacies an outgoing governor could leave behind. “Lagos is going to change governors without a quarrel. In May, one governor will hand to another a state that is whole. There is no greater gift a governor can leave his people than a handover that does not break the house,” he said. He urged Hamzat and his running mate, Princess Damilola Sonayon-James, to maintain close engagement with residents, complete ongoing infrastructure projects and sustain the state’s development framework. Sanwo-Olu also called on APC members to mobilise support across the state’s wards, while urging residents to scrutinise the manifesto and make informed choices ahead of the 2027 elections. Presenting his manifesto, Hamzat unveiled a seven-pillar development agenda, tagged PROMISE, which he said would guide his administration if elected. The acronym represents People First, Renewal, Opportunity, Machinery of Government, Inclusion, Security and Resilience, and Everyday Dignity. He said the agenda was designed to consolidate the achievements of successive APC administrations while addressing the challenges of a rapidly expanding megacity through inclusive growth, efficient service delivery and improved living standards. Describing a promise as a responsibility, Hamzat said: “A promise is a debt. In Yoruba, we say: Gbese ni Ileri. A promise has weight.” He identified respect, work and truth as the principles that would guide his proposed administration, adding that the manifesto contained specific commitments against which residents could assess his performance. Hamzat said his understanding of governance was shaped by his upbringing, particularly his father’s involvement in the administration of former Governor Lateef Jakande, as well as his own experience in public service. He recalled growing up in Mushin, where he witnessed challenges such as poor drainage and unreliable electricity, adding that the experiences had influenced his commitment to responsive governance. On healthcare, the APC candidate promised to increase the number of Maternal and Child Centres from 10 to 15 and expand the Ilera Eko health insurance scheme to cover one in three Lagos residents, with priority given to low-income households. He also pledged to build two new general hospitals in Ogombo and Ibeju-Lekki, upgrade 100 primary healthcare centres to flagship status and recruit more doctors, nurses and midwives to strengthen the state’s healthcare workforce. Hamzat further highlighted ongoing hospital projects, including the 150-bed Massey Children’s Hospital, the 280-bed Ojo General Hospital and the 150-bed Somolu General Hospital. In education, he promised to strengthen the EKOEXCEL programme, which operates in 1,028 public primary schools, and expand access to quality education from early childhood to university level. He also proposed establishing a University of Medicine and Health Sciences to train more healthcare professionals and provide opportunities for them to develop their careers in Lagos. The candidate pledged sustained investment in teacher development, noting that more than 33,000 teachers had been trained in the state over the past seven years. He also promised to reactivate the proposed multi-billion-dollar Fourth Mainland Bridge project. Hamzat said his manifesto built on the current administration’s THEMES Plus agenda and the Federal Government’s Renewed Hope Agenda, while outlining his proposed priorities for healthcare, education, economic development, infrastructure and social welfare. The post Sanwo-Olu urges Lagosians to trust Hamzat, avoid experiment appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Emery’s focus fully on Fulham despite Barcelona tie
items.description: Aston Villa manager Unai Emery has said Fulham will have his complete attention on Saturday despite next week’s high-profile Champions League tie away to Barcelona. Villa will be bidding for their third successive win in the Premier League against the Cottagers before taking on Spanish champions Barcelona in Europe. “If I am thinking, if we are thinking, after the match tomorrow against Fulham, we are making a mistake, and we are wrong, completely wrong,” Emery told reporters on Friday ahead of the match at Villa Park. “So, tomorrow, Fulham, prioritising Premier League clearly, and this is the message,” said the Spaniard, whose side ended leaders Manchester City’s perfect start to the season with a 2-1 win last week. “To keep our consistency, to keep our demands and work every day. To get this commitment to keep our consistency like we did last year. Each match is a test. “In the Premier League, we lack points. Of course, we are progressing, we are getting better. But, if we want to be consistent like last year and in the top positions, we must focus on tomorrow’s match, prioritising 100 percent and focusing, respecting them (Fulham).” Birmingham club Villa are currently ninth in the Premier League table, three points ahead of London side Fulham. Ces réseaux spécialisés dans le trafic de stupéfiants ont été démantelés à la suite de deux opérations de descente ciblées, précise une source cité par Mosaïque FM, ce vendredi 30 octobre 2026. items.title: Zamfara shows transformational leadership under Lawal — EFCC chairman
items.description: The Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Mr Ola Olukoyede, has described developments in Zamfara State under Governor Dauda Lawal as evidence of transformational leadership. Olukoyede spoke on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the 30th anniversary lecture of Zamfara State, held at the Grand Chamber of the Government House in Gusau. He said he accepted the invitation to speak at the event after conducting personal checks on the governor and the state’s development trajectory, particularly over the past three years. The EFCC chairman explained that his office’s ethical demands generally kept him away from political events and government houses, but that what he discovered about Zamfara persuaded him to attend. “By virtue of the ethical demands of my office, I don’t attend political events; I don’t go to the government house as a matter of principle. But when I received this invitation, something told me to accept and see what was going on there,” he said. Olukoyede said he had also discussed his findings with President Bola Tinubu, who encouraged him to attend the anniversary celebration. He said his arrival in Gusau offered him an opportunity to observe some of the infrastructure projects and changes taking place in the state. “As I arrived in Gusau, the first thing I noticed was the new airport. It is noticeable even to first-time visitors. The capital city speaks of visible transformation, as we have seen. Newly paved roads align with street solar lights,” he said. According to him, Zamfara had for years remained among Nigeria’s less-developed states despite its natural potential and efforts by successive administrations. He, however, said the state’s outlook was changing, adding that the physical development of Gusau reflected broader changes across Zamfara. The EFCC chairman also commended the state government’s reported progress in education, particularly its performance in national examinations conducted by the National Examinations Council (NECO) and the West African Examinations Council (WAEC). He attributed the developments to what he described as deliberate reform initiatives by the Lawal administration, noting that they aligned with the anniversary lecture’s theme, “Accountability and Responsibility in Transformational Government”. Olukoyede said the decision to invite the EFCC chairman to address the state anniversary reflected the governor’s commitment to transparency and accountability. In his remarks, Governor Lawal said the anniversary theme, “Reflections, Achievements, and the Future”, was designed to provide an opportunity to examine the challenges that had shaped the state’s journey and consider the responsibilities of leaders in securing a better future. He said the anniversary lecture had provided a platform for intellectual engagement on critical issues, including public accountability, community participation in tackling insecurity, preservation of history and culture, and the relationship between security and socio-economic development. Lawal said the discussions were central to his administration’s development agenda, particularly its Six-Point Rescue Agenda and the Zamfara State Development Plan 2025–2034. According to him, the development plan provides a long-term framework for the state’s economic growth, infrastructure, social welfare, human capital development, governance and environmental sustainability. “We must turn these commitments into measurable improvements in people’s lives,” the governor said. He expressed appreciation to the speakers, discussants, organising committee and other participants for their contributions to the anniversary programme. Other speakers at the anniversary lecture included Professors Tijjani Muhammad Bande, Sulaiman Kura, Murtala Rufai and Taofik Aminu. The post Zamfara shows transformational leadership under Lawal — EFCC chairman appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Pakistan: Rights Lawyers Receive 10-Year Sentences
items.description: Click to expand Image Human rights lawyers Imaan Mazari (right) and Hadi Ali Chattha, during a court hearing in Islamabad, Pakistan, December 5, 2025. © 2025 Aamir Qureshi/AFP via Getty Images (New York) – An anti-terrorism court in Pakistan imposed 10-year prison sentences on two human rights lawyers on October 29, 2026, in an escalation of the government’s crackdown on civil society, Human Rights Watch said today. Pakistani authorities should immediately quash the convictions, release Imaan Mazari-Hazir and her husband Hadi Ali Chattha, and cease criminal proceedings aimed at punishing human rights advocates. The sentences were handed down following a trial held inside Adiala prison in Rawalpindi. The lawyers were accused of obstructing police at a road closure in Islamabad in October 2024. Instead of prosecuting them for a misdemeanor or common crime, the police charged them under Pakistan’s anti-terrorism act, which carries far greater penalties and a longer sentence. This was the second time in recent weeks that the two have been prosecuted in an apparent attempt to prevent them from carrying out their legal work. “Prosecuting two human rights lawyers for terrorism sends a chilling message to everyone who speaks up for fundamental rights in Pakistan,” said Patricia Gossman, senior associate Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “The authorities should quash the outrageous 10-year sentences handed down to Imaan Mazari-Hazir and Hadi Ali Chattha.” Mazari and Chattha have represented journalists as well as political and human rights activists. They have defended people facing blasphemy charges, victims of sexual violence and enforced disappearances, and prisoners facing the death penalty. In addition, the court sentenced both lawyers to three years in prison for “obstructing and assaulting public servants,” to run concurrently. Family members allege that during the trial, Mazari and Chattha were denied legal representation of their choice and access to key legal documents, raising serious concerns about the fairness of the trial, due process, and the right to prepare and present an effective defense. On September 17, the Supreme Court had suspended their sentences in a separate case involving social media posts and ordered their release on bail, but police rearrested them hours later. On September 30, United Nations human rights experts called for their immediate release and said that successive proceedings appeared intended to punish them for their views and their human rights advocacy. Pakistani authorities have used vague and overbroad anti-terrorism legislation to sentence and imprison those protesting government policies. The authorities should prosecute alleged violence under appropriate criminal laws while protecting the rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly. Allegations of obstructing officials or disrupting public order should not be treated as terrorism, Human Rights Watch said. The authorities should ensure that counterterrorism laws are narrowly drawn and applied and are not used to punish dissent or circumvent fair-trial protections. The UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers provide that governments should protect lawyers from intimidation, harassment, and improper interference, as well as from prosecution for carrying out recognized professional duties. “Punishing lawyers and human rights activists for defending rights leaves those they represent without protection,” Gossman said. “Concerned governments should press Pakistan to end its crackdown on human rights advocacy.”

items.title: Sahara marocain : la Russie oppose son veto au projet de résolution
items.description: Le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU a rejeté, ce vendredi à New York, le texte porté par Washington sur le Sahara. Onze membres l’ont soutenu, mais le vote négatif de la Russie, membre permanent, suffit à le faire tomber, à la veille de l’expiration du mandat de la mission onusienne. Le scrutin s’est soldé par onze voix favorables, trois abstentions et une voix contre. Celle-ci émane de la Russie, qui détient un droit de veto. La présidence du Conseil, assurée ce mois-ci par la Grèce, a donc constaté que le projet américain n’était pas adopté. Les États-Unis, rédacteurs du texte dans ce dossier, avaient pourtant remanié leur copie à plusieurs reprises dans l’espoir d’écarter ce scénario. Le revers est d’autant plus marqué qu’il intervient un an, presque jour pour jour, après l’adoption de la résolution 2797, qui avait recueilli onze voix et les abstentions de la Russie, de la Chine et du Pakistan. Cette fois, Moscou a choisi de s’opposer plutôt que de s’abstenir. L’Algérie, qui ne siège plus au Conseil depuis janvier, avait été conviée à la séance, sans droit de vote. Veto russe au Conseil de sécurité sur le Sahara. 11 pour : États-Unis, France, Royaume-Uni, Danemark, Grèce, Panama, Bahreïn, Colombie, Lettonie, Liberia, RD Congo 3 abstentions : Chine, Pakistan, Somalie 1 contre : … pic.twitter.com/CrrfdluI17 — Sahara Policy Index (@saharapolicy) October 30, 2026 The post Sahara marocain : la Russie oppose son veto au projet de résolution appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Naira appreciates to N1,373/$ in parallel market
items.description: By Elizabeth Adegbesan The naira today appreciated to N1,373 per dollar from N1,380 in the parallel market on Thursday. But the naira was stable at N1,346 per dollar in the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), data from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) showed. Consequently, the margin between the parallel and official markets narrowed to N27 per dollar from N36 per dollar on Thursday. The value of interbank turnover in NFEM increased by 8.9 per cent to $58.9 billion from $54.05 billion on Thursday. Analysts expect the mixed performance of the naira in the following weeks. In their financial market review and outlook, analysts at Cowry Asset Management Limited said, “Going forward, we expect the naira to remain relatively mixed across the foreign exchange markets in the near term, supported by marginal improvements in external reserves and potential foreign exchange inflows. “However, sustained pressure on foreign currency demand could limit further gains.” The post Naira appreciates to N1,373/$ in parallel market appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Journalisme en Afrique : 61 % des journalistes peinent à couvrir leurs besoins essentiels
items.description: La précarité économique, les menaces et les restrictions à la liberté de la presse fragilisent le journalisme sur le continent africain. Dans un rapport portant sur 1 586 journalistes issus de 45 pays, la Fédération des journalistes africains (FAJ) alerte sur la dégradation des conditions de travail et la progression de l’autocensure. La pauvreté, l’insécurité et la censure plongent le journalisme africain dans une crise profonde. C’est le constat dressé par la Fédération des journalistes africains (FAJ) dans son premier rapport continental intitulé « Le journalisme assiégé : conditions de travail épouvantables et déclin de la liberté de la presse en Afrique », exploité par nos confrères de l'APS. Réalisée auprès de 1 586 journalistes dans 45 pays couvrant les cinq régions du continent, avec l’appui du Programme multi-donateurs de l’UNESCO sur la liberté d’expression et la sécurité des journalistes, cette étude met en évidence les difficultés économiques, professionnelles et sécuritaires auxquelles sont confrontés les acteurs des médias. « Les conclusions de ce rapport mettent en lumière une profession en crise profonde. On attend des journalistes qu’ils informent le public alors qu’ils luttent pour survivre », a déclaré Omar Faruk Osman, président de la FAJ, dans un communiqué transmis à l’APS. Les difficultés financières constituent l’une des principales préoccupations. Selon le rapport, 61 % des journalistes interrogés affirment que leurs revenus ne leur permettent pas de couvrir leurs besoins essentiels. Seuls 4 % estiment que leur rémunération suffit à prendre en charge leurs dépenses de base. À cette précarité s’ajoutent des conditions d’emploi souvent instables. Cinquante-huit pour cent des personnes interrogées déclarent subir des retards de paiement de leur salaire, tandis que 62 % travaillent sans contrat écrit et 71 % ne bénéficient d’aucune protection sociale. Les pigistes représentent 29 % de l’échantillon, auxquels s’ajoutent 18 % de collaborateurs et de correspondants indépendants. Pour le président de la FAJ, ces difficultés économiques et professionnelles compromettent directement l’exercice du métier. « Lorsque les journalistes ne peuvent pas gagner leur vie, travailler en toute sécurité ou rendre compte librement, la liberté de la presse n’existe que sur le papier », a-t-il souligné. L’autocensure gagne du terrain Au-delà des difficultés économiques, les journalistes africains font face à des menaces susceptibles de limiter leur liberté éditoriale. Selon l’enquête, 65 % des répondants ont subi des menaces ou des actes d’intimidation liés à leur travail au cours des trois dernières années. Seuls 17 % déclarent se sentir toujours en sécurité dans l’exercice de leur profession, contre 55 % qui se sentent rarement ou jamais en sécurité. Le rapport indique également qu’au moins 18 journalistes et professionnels des médias ont été tués en Afrique en 2025 en raison de leur activité professionnelle. Ces pressions ont des répercussions sur le traitement de l’information. Ainsi, 84 % des journalistes interrogés déclarent pratiquer fréquemment ou occasionnellement l’autocensure. De même, 69 % affirment avoir renoncé à traiter certains sujets en raison de menaces. L’ingérence politique arrive en tête des menaces les plus graves pour la liberté de la presse, citée par 29 % des répondants. Elle est suivie de la violence contre les journalistes (22 %) et des lois restrictives (18 %). Les violations rapportées illustrent l’ampleur des obstacles rencontrés : 68 % des personnes interrogées signalent des ingérences politiques, 61 % des difficultés d’accès à l’information, 57 % des actes de censure et 49 % des formes d’intimidation judiciaire. Les coupures d’Internet affectant le travail journalistique concernent, quant à elles, 23 % des répondants. Au total, seuls 6 % des journalistes interrogés considèrent que la liberté de la presse est « très libre » dans leur pays, tandis que 65 % la jugent restreinte ou fortement restreinte. Les risques numériques et le mal-être professionnel Les menaces s’étendent également à l’environnement numérique. Trente-six pour cent des journalistes interrogés déclarent avoir subi du harcèlement en ligne lié à leur activité, 26 % font état de surveillance numérique, 24 % d’abus sexuels en ligne et 21 % de tentatives de piratage. Malgré ces risques, 63 % indiquent n’avoir bénéficié d’aucune formation en matière de sécurité numérique. Les femmes journalistes sont particulièrement exposées. Selon 76 % des répondants, elles font face à des risques supplémentaires, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, les violences en ligne fondées sur le genre, les inégalités salariales, la discrimination professionnelle et l’exclusion des postes à responsabilité. Le rapport met aussi en évidence les conséquences de ces conditions de travail sur la santé mentale et la pérennité de la profession. L’insécurité financière constitue la principale source de stress, citée par 38 % des répondants, devant la peur des agressions (24 %). Par ailleurs, 72 % déclarent que leur employeur ne propose aucun soutien en matière de santé mentale ou d’accompagnement psychologique. Quarante-quatre pour cent signalent un épuisement professionnel fréquent, tandis que 47 % ont déjà envisagé de quitter le journalisme. Plus de la moitié des personnes interrogées, soit 53 %, sont âgées de 18 à 34 ans. Pour la FAJ, le départ de ces jeunes professionnels pourrait fragiliser davantage le journalisme d’investigation, le contrôle de l’action publique et l’accès des citoyens à une information fiable. Face à cette situation, l’organisation appelle les gouvernements, les employeurs des médias et les institutions concernées à prendre des mesures urgentes. Elle préconise notamment des rémunérations équitables, la formalisation des contrats de travail, l’accès à la protection sociale et la garantie de conditions de travail sûres. Le rapport recommande également des enquêtes rapides sur les agressions contre les journalistes, la lutte contre l’impunité, la réforme des lois utilisées pour intimider les professionnels des médias et le renforcement des mécanismes de protection. Il insiste enfin sur la nécessité de préserver l’indépendance éditoriale, de promouvoir le dialogue social et de mettre en place des dispositifs spécifiques de protection des femmes journalistes.

items.title: L’essor de l’IA fait vaciller Google en Bourse, près de 500 milliards de dollars envolés
items.description: La maison mère de Google, Alphabet, a connu l’une des plus importantes chutes boursières de l’histoire après avoir perdu plus de 12 % de sa valeur en une seule séance, soit près de 500 milliards de dollars de capitalisation. En cause : des résultats trimestriels inférieurs aux attentes, notamment dans la publicité, sur fond d’inquiétudes concernant l’impact de l’intelligence artificielle sur le modèle économique historique du géant américain. L’intelligence artificielle pourrait-elle fragiliser le modèle économique de Google ? C’est l’une des questions qui préoccupent désormais les investisseurs. Jeudi 29 octobre, Alphabet, maison mère du célèbre moteur de recherche, a subi une chute spectaculaire à Wall Street, avec une baisse de plus de 12 % de son action, effaçant près de 500 milliards de dollars de sa capitalisation boursière. Selon le magazine Forbes, il s'agit de la deuxième plus importante perte de valeur boursière enregistrée en une seule journée par une entreprise cotée, derrière celle de Nvidia en 2025. Cette dégringolade intervient après la publication des résultats financiers du troisième trimestre 2026, qui n'ont pas répondu aux attentes des marchés. Si le chiffre d'affaires du groupe a progressé de 25 % sur un an pour atteindre 127,6 milliards de dollars, il est resté légèrement inférieur aux 128 milliards anticipés par les analystes. Le bénéfice net a, quant à lui, reculé de 25 %, à 26,2 milliards de dollars. Cette baisse s'explique principalement par un effet comptable lié à la valorisation des participations du groupe, notamment à la suite du recul du cours des actions de SpaceX, qui a pesé à hauteur de 8,7 milliards de dollars. La publicité, premier point de fragilité Au cœur des inquiétudes figure le ralentissement de l'activité publicitaire, qui constitue historiquement l'un des principaux moteurs financiers de Google. Au troisième trimestre, les revenus publicitaires ont progressé de 11 %, un rythme inférieur aux attentes des analystes, qui tablaient sur une croissance proche de 13 %. Cette évolution intervient dans un contexte de transformation profonde des usages numériques. La montée en puissance des outils d'intelligence artificielle générative modifie progressivement la manière dont les internautes recherchent des informations, découvrent des produits et accèdent aux contenus en ligne. Les investisseurs redoutent notamment que les assistants conversationnels et les agents autonomes d'intelligence artificielle détournent une partie du trafic du moteur de recherche traditionnel. Une évolution qui pourrait, à terme, remettre en question le modèle publicitaire sur lequel Google a construit une grande partie de sa domination. La progression des nouveaux acteurs de l'IA, dont OpenAI, qui développe également ses propres activités publicitaires, renforce ces interrogations. Tout n'est cependant pas négatif dans les résultats d'Alphabet. Son activité de cloud computing affiche une dynamique particulièrement forte, portée par l'explosion des besoins en infrastructures nécessaires au développement de l'intelligence artificielle. Les revenus de cette branche ont progressé de 102 % sur un an, après une hausse de 82 % au trimestre précédent. Il s'agit de sa plus forte croissance en cinq ans. Lors de la présentation des résultats, le directeur général d'Alphabet, Sundar Pichai, a souligné l'ampleur de la demande en capacités informatiques et en centres de données. Le carnet de commandes de l'activité cloud atteignait ainsi 561 milliards de dollars à la fin du mois de septembre. Le groupe entend poursuivre ses investissements pour augmenter ses capacités et répondre à cette demande croissante. The post L’essor de l’IA fait vaciller Google en Bourse, près de 500 milliards de dollars envolés appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Théâtre tunisien | La 4e édition des « Saisons de la Création » célèbre Mohamed Driss et Taoufik Jebali
items.description: La quatrième édition du Festival National du Théâtre Tunisien « Les Saisons de la Création » rend hommage à deux figures majeures de la scène nationale, Mohamed Driss et Taoufik Jebali. Mohamed Driss et Taoufik Jebali… Deux parcours majeurs de la mémoire théâtrale tunisienne à l’honneur de la quatrième édition du Festival National du Théâtre Tunisien « Les Saisons de la Création ». En hommage à deux parcours artistiques qui ont contribué à façonner le théâtre tunisien moderne, à enrichir ses expériences créatives et à développer ses institutions, la quatrième édition du Festival National du Théâtre Tunisien « Les Saisons de la Création » rend hommage aux artistes et metteurs en scène Mohamed Driss et Taoufik Jebali, en reconnaissance de leurs contributions à la création théâtrale, au développement des arts de la scène, à la formation et à la transmission aux nouvelles générations. Cette édition consacre une partie de son programme à la projection de plusieurs œuvres théâtrales filmées de Mohamed Driss et Taoufik Jebali, dans le cadre de la rubrique « Écrans des Saisons », offrant ainsi au public l’occasion de redécouvrir différentes étapes de leurs parcours artistiques et des facettes de leurs œuvres théâtrales. Un rendez-vous spécial sera également organisé autour des deux artistes, avec des témoignages vivants qui évoqueront leurs parcours et leurs expériences artistiques et humaines, tout en mettant en lumière leurs contributions à l’enrichissement de la scène théâtrale tunisienne et leur empreinte auprès de plusieurs générations de professionnels du théâtre. Cette édition revient ainsi sur deux parcours complémentaires par la diversité de leurs expériences et de leurs formes d’expression. De la contribution de Mohamed Driss à la fondation du Nouveau Théâtre et à son travail à la tête du Théâtre National Tunisien, à l'expérience de Taoufik Jebali dans l'écriture, la mise en scène et l'interprétation, ainsi que la fondation de l'espace El Teatro, se dessinent plusieurs étapes de l'histoire du théâtre tunisien moderne, marquées par la recherche, l'expérimentation, le renouvellement et la création d'institutions et d'espaces de formation. La quatrième édition ouvre ses représentations avec le spectacle « Le Fou », mis en scène par Taoufik Jebali, renouant ainsi avec une œuvre de son parcours créatif. Cette rencontre sera l'occasion de célébrer deux itinéraires artistiques qui ont durablement marqué la mémoire théâtrale tunisienne. L’article Théâtre tunisien | La 4e édition des « Saisons de la Création » célèbre Mohamed Driss et Taoufik Jebali est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: Sahara occidental : à quelques heures du vote, la Russie présente un projet concurrent face à Washington
items.description: À quelques heures du vote au Conseil de sécurité, la Russie a décidé de présenter un projet de résolution concurrent à celui des États-Unis. Cette initiative intervient dans un contexte de fortes divergences sur l’avenir de la MINURSO et les orientations du processus politique au Sahara occidental . Le projet russe prévoit une simple prorogation du mandat de la MINURSO jusqu’au 31 octobre 2027, sans modifier son mandat ni ses prérogatives. Le projet réaffirme la recherche d’un règlement juste, durable et mutuellement acceptable, conformément à la Charte des Nations unies, notamment au principe de l’autodétermination. Sahara occidental : pourquoi la Russie présente un projet de résolution Cette initiative rejoint plusieurs réserves exprimées par la Chine et le Pakistan. Pékin défend le maintien du mandat et du nom de la MINURSO, des négociations sur un pied d’égalité et le respect de l’ensemble des résolutions pertinentes du Conseil. Islamabad plaide pour une solution politique fondée sur le dialogue, le consensus entre les parties et le droit à l’autodétermination. En présentant un texte concurrent, Moscou ne cherchait pas nécessairement à imposer une résolution alternative mais cette démarche lui permettait de contester une réorientation de la mission décidée sous impulsion américaine, sans véritable consensus au Conseil. Elle offrait également à la Russie, à la Chine et au Pakistan un argument supplémentaire pour justifier leur abstention. L’article Sahara occidental : à quelques heures du vote, la Russie présente un projet concurrent face à Washington est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: US midterm early voting hits record 48 million
items.description: A record 47.9 million Americans have already voted in next week’s US midterm elections, with participation surging in key battleground states and registered Democrats outpacing Republicans, figures showed Friday. The University of Florida’s Election Lab had recorded 47,922,669 early votes nationwide by midday, surpassing the previous midterm record of 45.9 million cast ahead of Election Day in 2022. The surge is especially pronounced in states with fiercely contested Senate races that could determine control of the chamber during the final two years of President Donald Trump’s presidency. In Texas, more than six million people had voted early by Wednesday, according to official figures, with in-person turnout running around 50 percent ahead of the same stage in 2022. North Carolina’s election board reported early voting up nearly 37 percent on the same point four years ago, while South Carolina surpassed its entire 2022 early vote total on Monday, with five days of early voting still to go. In Kansas, where Republican Senator Roger Marshall faces a tough re-election fight, advance ballots were running around two-thirds ahead of 2022 last week, according to the secretary of state’s office. In states that record voters’ party affiliation, registered Democrats have accounted for a substantially larger share of early ballots than Republicans. Election Lab figures showed Democrats making up around 44 percent of early voters in those states, compared with 31 percent for Republicans and 25 percent for unaffiliated or minor-party voters. University of Florida political scientist Michael McDonald, who oversees the Election Lab, has pointed to rising participation among Black and Hispanic voters in states that report racial and ethnic data, with particularly strong turnout in heavily Hispanic communities along the Texas-Mexico border. In Georgia, where early in-person voting broke the state’s midterm record on Thursday, women accounted for 56 percent of ballots cast by that day, compared with 44 percent for men. “Georgians continue to head to the polls in record numbers because they trust the system,” top elections official Brad Raffensperger said Thursday. But experts warn against interpreting the figures as a prediction of the election outcome. A voter’s party registration does not reveal which candidates they supported, and tens of millions more Americans are expected to cast ballots on Tuesday. In recent elections Republicans have tended to turn out in greater numbers on Election Day, potentially narrowing or reversing the Democrats’ early advantage. And higher early participation does not necessarily translate into higher overall turnout, since some voters may simply be casting ballots sooner than in previous elections. items.title: UGB de Saint-Louis : le CROUS et le Cadre de Vie signent une convention pour un campus plus accueillant
items.description: Le Centre régional des œuvres universitaires de Saint-Louis (Crous) et la Direction générale du Cadre de Vie veulent donner un nouveau souffle à l’environnement de l’Université Gaston-Berger. Les deux institutions ont signé jeudi, une convention de partenariat pour renforcer les actions de propreté, d’aménagement et d’entretien du campus avec l’ambition d’offrir aux étudiants un cadre de vie plus agréable. Le Crous de Saint-Louis et la Direction générale du Cadre de Vie ont décidé de conjuguer leurs efforts pour un campus plus propre, bien aménagé et accueillant. La convention de partenariat a été signée par le directeur du CROUS, Thierno Mbaye, et le directeur général du Cadre de Vie, Bouna Seck en présence de leurs collaborateurs. Pour Thierno Mbaye, cette collaboration vient renforcer les initiatives déjà engagées pour améliorer le quotidien des pensionnaires de l’Université Gaston-Berger. Il rappelle que la vie universitaire ne se déroule pas uniquement dans les salles de cours et les amphithéâtres. Elle se poursuit dans les villages étudiants, les espaces de restauration et les lieux de rencontre. « Les étudiants y passent une grande partie de leur temps. Il est donc important qu’ils puissent évoluer dans un environnement propre, agréable et bien entretenu », a-t-il souligné. Le directeur du Crous estime que la qualité du cadre de vie fait pleinement partie de la mission de son institution. « Prendre soin du campus, c’est aussi prendre soin des étudiants », a-t-il insisté, appelant à une mobilisation de toute la communauté universitaire pour préserver les espaces communs. De son côté, Bouna Seck voit dans cette convention une opportunité de donner une nouvelle impulsion à l'amélioration du cadre de vie à Saint-Louis. Il estime que les actions engagées à l'Ugb peuvent également avoir des retombées positives sur la ville et les autres communes de la région. Le directeur général du Cadre de Vie a rappelé la mission que lui a confiée le chef de l'État lors de sa nomination : « Je vous donne le quotidien des Sénégalais. » Une responsabilité qui, selon lui, doit se traduire par des changements visibles dans l'environnement des populations. A l'université de Saint-Louis, cette ambition passe notamment par des espaces plus agréables, des aménagements adaptés et une meilleure organisation du campus. Bouna Seck souhaite faire de l'Ugb un lieu attractif où les étudiants peuvent apprendre, se retrouver et profiter d'un environnement propice à leur épanouissement. Les équipes du Crous et du Cadre de Vie devront ainsi travailler ensemble pour identifier les besoins et les interventions prioritaires. L'entretien des sites, le pavage, l'aménagement des espaces verts et l'organisation des cantines figurent parmi les questions à examiner. Le directeur général a également invité les étudiants à participer à cette dynamique, notamment en contribuant aux initiatives d'amélioration et de préservation de leur environnement. A travers cette convention, les deux institutions entendent donner une dimension plus concrète à leurs engagements. Pour Thierno Mbaye, l'essentiel reste que les étudiants puissent constater, dans leur vie quotidienne, les effets de cette collaboration. Jeanne SAGNA (Correspondante)

items.description: ISLAMABAD: The Directorate of Building Control (City) of the Capital Development Authority (CDA) on Friday issued a warning notice to remove within 15 days a guards’ room and “unauthorised and illegal” construction at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in the federal capital’s posh G-6 sector. The notice affixed outside the residence of the JUI-F chief — addressed to the legal owner of the property and dated Oct 30 (Friday) — highlighted three violations under the Islamabad Capital Territory Building Control Regulations 2020 (amended 2023). It pointed out illegal and unauthorised construction in building setbacks (open spaces), a guard post built on CDA land, and a generator on CDA land. The notice added that according to records, the owner submitted an affidavit on March 18, 2019, at the time of issuance of a no-objection certificate (NOC), in which he stated that setback violations would be removed within three months and all regulations would be abided by. “However, it has been noticed that no compliance is made,” the CDA notice said. The authority directed that the mentioned violations be removed within 15 days, starting Friday. The city manager warned that if the occupants failed to fulfil the legal requirements and remove the violations, the CDA would take action as per the relevant clauses of the CDA Ordinance and Islamabad Capital Territory Building Control Regulations 2020 (amended 2023), which it warned could lead to the sealing or demolishing of violations as well as the initiation of a case for cancellation of the allotment. Meanwhile, after the notice was issued, Maulana Asjad Mahmood, the son of the JUI-F chief, claimed it was retaliation for pointing out alleged encroachments by a senior military official. In a statement, Mahmood said that instead of responding to the alleged encroachments, the authorities resorted to what he described as underhanded tactics. He expressed concern over the “transformation of political differences into personal revenge”. He said such actions were a matter of serious concern and urged the nation and JUI-F workers to remain informed and vigilant about the evolving situation.

items.title: Fête de l’Unité : grâce royale au profit de 907 personnes
items.description: A l'occasion de la Première Commémoration de la Fête de l’Unité, le Roi Mohammed VI a bien voulu accorder sa grâce à 907 personnes, dont 613 en détention et 294 en liberté, condamnées par différents tribunaux du Royaume, annonce le ministère de la Justice dans un communiqué. En voici le texte : « A l'occasion de la Première Commémoration de la Fête de l’Unité de cette année 1448H-2026G, Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu perpétue Sa gloire, a bien voulu accorder Sa grâce à un ensemble de personnes condamnées par différents tribunaux du Royaume. Ces personnes sont au nombre de 907 et se présentent comme suit: *Les bénéficiaires de la Grâce Royale qui sont en détention sont au nombre de 613 détenus se répartissant comme suit: -Grâce sur le reliquat de la peine d’emprisonnement ou de réclusion au profit de 17 détenus. -Remise de la peine d’emprisonnement ou de réclusion au profit de 595 détenus. -Commutation de la peine perpétuelle en peine à temps au profit de 01 détenu. *Les bénéficiaires de la Grâce Royale qui sont en liberté sont au nombre de 294 personnes se répartissant comme suit : -Grâce sur la peine d’emprisonnement ou son reliquat au profit de 72 personnes. -Grâce sur la peine d’emprisonnement avec maintien de l’amende au profit de 09 personnes. -Grâce sur la peine d’amende au profit de 202 personnes. -Grâce sur la peine d’emprisonnement et d’amende au profit de 11 personnes. Puisse Dieu garder Sa Majesté le Roi, source de clémence et de miséricorde, perpétuer Sa gloire et préserver Son Altesse Royale le Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan, ainsi que tous les membres de la Famille Royale ». items.title: Nouvelle aide militaire de l’union européenne à la Mauritanie : 20 millions d’euros pour renforcer la capacité de la surveillance de son territoire
items.description: L'Union européenne a porté le montant de son aide militaire à la Mauritanie à 75 millions d'euros, après l'adoption d'un nouveau volet de 20 millions d'euros destiné à fournir du matériel non militaire afin de renforcer les capacités de l'armée en matière de surveillance du territoire. Le Conseil de l’Union européenne a déclaré dans un communiqué que ce nouveau programme, le quatrième dans le cadre de la Facilité européenne pour la paix, fournira aux forces armées mauritaniennes des équipements supplémentaires de surveillance terrestre, en complément de ceux déjà approuvés dans le programme de 2025. Le Conseil a ajouté que cette aide vise à soutenir les capacités de l’armée mauritanienne à surveiller la situation dans différentes régions du pays, dans le cadre des efforts visant à renforcer la stabilité dans la région du Sahel et à réduire les risques de déstabilisation, à protéger la souveraineté de la Mauritanie, l’intégrité de son territoire et la sécurité de sa population civile. Les programmes d’aide européens précédents comprenaient des équipements et des capacités militaires destinés aux opérations terrestres et maritimes, notamment en matière de surveillance et de dissuasion.

items.title: Lfr 2026 : le gouvernement précise ses choix budgétaires
items.description: Le gouvernement a apporté des réponses aux préoccupations soulevées par la Commission des finances et du contrôle budgétaire dans son mémorandum du 26 octobre 2026, relatif au projet de loi de finances rectificative (Lfr) pour l’année 2026. Dans ce document daté du 29 octobre, le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan détaille notamment les contraintes budgétaires, le financement du déficit, les subventions à l’énergie et le règlement des arriérés de paiement. S’agissant des équilibres budgétaires, l’État maintient le plafond du déficit à 1 735,2 milliards de FCFA, soit 7,6 % du produit intérieur brut (PIB). Le gouvernement précise que ce montant constitue une autorisation maximale et non une prévision de l’exécution définitive. Il invoque notamment les incertitudes entourant les recettes attendues au dernier trimestre, la volatilité des cours du pétrole et la nécessité d’honorer les engagements envers les entreprises pour éviter l’accumulation de nouveaux arriérés. Concernant le secteur de l’énergie, l’enveloppe globale prévue atteint 790,3 milliards de FCfa, dont 718,3 milliards destinés au Fonds spécial de soutien au secteur de l’énergie (Fse) et 72 milliards au Cerp. Selon le gouvernement, les ressources supplémentaires doivent notamment permettre de sécuriser l’approvisionnement en hydrocarbures et la production d’électricité, tout en évitant une répercussion de la hausse des coûts sur les consommateurs. Le document revient également sur les transferts sociaux. Une enveloppe de 70 milliards de FCfa est prévue à ce titre, dont 48 milliards mobilisés à travers le Cerp. Le nombre de ménages bénéficiaires des bourses de sécurité familiale devrait ainsi passer de 355 013 à 469 497. Sur la question des arriérés de paiement, l’État indique qu’un inventaire de l’Inspection générale des finances a recensé, au 31 décembre 2024, des arriérés de 2 494,9 milliards de FCfa portant sur 6 497 dossiers. Après le règlement de 538,6 milliards en 2025, le reliquat s’établit à 1 956,3 milliards de FCFA, répartis entre 5 425 dossiers. Le gouvernement distingue les dossiers réguliers, évalués à 967,8 milliards, de ceux présentant des irrégularités ou des pièces justificatives manquantes, estimés à 988,5 milliards. Il assure que ces derniers ne seront pas payés avant les vérifications nécessaires. Pour le financement de la Lfr, les besoins globaux sont évalués à 6 774 milliards de FCfa. Le gouvernement présente un plan de financement reposant notamment sur les emprunts-programmes, les prêts-projets, les ressources du marché régional et d’autres concours financiers. Il avertit qu’un retard dans l’adoption du texte pourrait reporter à 2027 certains appuis budgétaires exceptionnels ainsi que des financements de projets et des prêts-programmes, avec des conséquences sur le bouclage du financement de l’exercice 2026. Enfin, concernant la taxe sur les activités financières appliquée aux transactions de mobile money, les recettes mobilisées à fin septembre 2026 atteignent 44,4 milliards de FCfa, dont 12,49 milliards correspondant à des régularisations relatives à la période d’octobre à décembre 2025. Hors ces régularisations, les recettes de 2026 s’élèvent à 31,91 milliards de FCfa sur les neuf premiers mois de l’année. Salla GUEYE

items.title: Hundreds evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky during rare Ukraine ceasefire
items.description: Hundreds of residents of the devastated Russian-occupied city of Oleshky have been evacuated, Russian and Ukrainian authorities have said, following a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. “Everything unfolded without any incidents, and both sides noted the high level of organisation,” Russia’s human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova said. Ukrainian authorities confirmed the evacuees were on their way to southern Russia, from where they will travel on to Ukraine through Belarus. Melania Trump said that “all elements of the convoy, including the safe passageway in and out of Oleshky, was established through mutual agreement between Russian and Ukrainian leaders”. Speaking to journalists on Friday evening, Lantratova put out a joint request with her Ukrainian counterpart “to the US First Lady… that humanitarian missions such as this one, delivering aid to residents in need, be conducted on a regular basis under the coordination of Mrs Melania Trump”. A ceasefire – the longest and most widespread since the start of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022 – has been in force in the entire frontline region of Kherson since Tuesday, allowing for the road out of Oleshky to be demined. Residents who wished to leave had a four-hour window to do so on Friday. A convoy of 25 buses was brought in to allow up to 750 people to leave the town until 14:00 (12:00 GMT), along with ambulances for people with limited mobility. Several hundred people are understood to have decided to stay, despite the widespread devastation and the lack of gas, electricity and running water. “Everyone who wishes to leave Oleshky will be given the opportunity to do so safely,” Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said on Friday morning. “At the same time, those who decide to remain will be able to stay and will receive all the necessary humanitarian assistance.” Ukrainian military positions lie 5km (3.1miles) from Oleshky, but the evacuees will first have to travel into Russian-occupied territory and then to the southern Russian city of Anapa. They will board a Russian government plane to Gomel in Belarus, and then drive across the border into Ukraine’s Chernihiv region. Others are expected to choose to stay in Russian-occupied territory. Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova travelled to Oleshky together on Friday, setting off from Armiansk, in the Russian-occupied Crimean peninsula. Lubinets is the first Ukrainian official since the start of the war to visit Russian-occupied parts of Ukraine. He will also become the first to visit Russia when he escorts the evacuees back into Ukraine on Saturday. The Oleshky ceasefire has required close cooperation with Lantratova, which Lubinets said he carried out in the interests of saving lives. But some in Ukraine have recoiled at the sight of him standing beside a representative of the Russian occupying power which has killed so many of the city’s residents and made life unbearable for the rest. Both Lubinets and Lantratova posted videos from Oleshky on their social media channels, saying people were given the chance to form two groups depending on whether they wanted to be taken to Russian-controlled territory or to Ukraine. In one video, Lubinets can be seen meeting tearful locals. “The problem is that a lot of people are staying,” he can be heard saying. “I was told that it was their own choice, we will do everything possible for the humanitarian aid to arrive.” Russia said on Thursday that it had prepared “dozens of tonnes” of aid for the residents who do not wish to leave, including food, medicine, hygiene products and fuel for generators. An Oleshky resident told the BBC she had decided against leaving because “they wouldn’t take my animals, so that’s it.” Olena, who now lives in Kyiv, said her grandmother and wider family in Oleshky were also staying behind. “The older generation does not want to leave,” she told the BBC. “I’ve barely managed to persuade my father – and only because I’ve just had a baby, who he would never see otherwise.” Olena’s grandmother’s sister died in Oleshky last winter. “She lost her legs after stepping on a landmine, covered in snow… People took her to the hospital in a garden wheelbarrow,” Olena said. “That’s how locals transport all wounded and dead people in Oleshky to the hospital and the hospital’s morgue: in garden wheelbarrows.” The ceasefire is due to be in force until the end of Sunday 1 November. It has provided the first few days of peace in the Kherson region since the start of Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Residents of Kherson told the BBC they were “overjoyed” by the ceasefire. However, they are concerned the truce has given Russia time to build up its military presence on the banks of the Dnipro river, which could result in a renewed assault once the ceasefire expires. On Friday, the Kremlin made it clear that the success of the Oleshky ceasefire should not be interpreted as willingness to extend the truce to the rest of Ukraine. A handful of foreign journalists have been invited to witness the evacuation of the town, which Moscow is expected to present as a humanitarian mission conducted with mercy to protect the people of Oleshky. Many Ukrainians suspect Russia’s real intention is to earn credit with the White House, and to provide US President Donald Trump with a boost ahead of next week’s midterm elections.

items.title: Petrol price unchanged, high-speed diesel raised by Rs2.29
items.description: The government on Friday raised the price of diesel by Rs2.29 per litre, but kept the petrol rate unchanged at Rs377.91. Following the revision, HSD will retail at Rs402.96 per litre. This is the second consecutive day the government kept the price of petrol unchanged. The prices are applicable from Oct 31 (Saturday) to Nov 2 (Monday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel. On Tuesday, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy. The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17 . For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then. Last week, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association had urged consumers not to resort to panic buying, as excessive purchases could create market distortions. Senators also raised concerns over fuel supply even after Minister of State for Finance and Revenue Bilal Azhar Kayani said that there were no supply issues. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months. On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices. Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: Ebola outbreak not under control in Africa, CDC warns
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has warned that the Ebola outbreak spreading across parts of Africa remains uncontrolled, with more than 10,200 confirmed cases and over 5,000 deaths recorded across the continent. The Director-General of Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, gave the warning on Friday during an interview on Channels Television’s Morning Brief programme, raising concerns about the continued transmission and changing geographical spread of the disease. Kaseya said the assessment followed a virtual ministerial meeting held on October 28, which brought together more than 42 ministers and over 600 participants, including representatives of international organisations and development partners, to review the outbreak and ongoing response efforts. “We analysed the data and we saw that the outbreak is not yet under control,” he said. He disclosed that the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) had recorded more than 10,000 confirmed infections, while the combined number of confirmed cases across the continent had exceeded 10,200. “We have achieved what is a number of 10,000 people confirmed cases in DRC and also, if we put together, it’s more than 10,200 confirmed cases across the continent,” Kaseya said. Kaseya said more than 5,000 people had died from the outbreak, although figures published by health authorities showed a slightly lower confirmed death toll. “We also saw that we have more than 5,000 people already passed on due to this outbreak,” he added. Kaseya also expressed concern over changes in the geographical spread of the disease, noting that its epicentre was shifting. The current outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus and has affected several African countries, including the DRC, Kenya and Nigeria. The DRC remains the worst-affected country, accounting for the overwhelming majority of infections and deaths. Data from the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control showed that the country had recorded 10,193 confirmed cases and 4,960 related deaths as of October 28. Kenya has also reported nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, following an imported infection linked to the DRC. Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case in more than a decade on October 20, after a 42-year-old Swiss woman tested positive for the Bundibugyo strain in Abuja. The woman, who had travelled from Uganda to Nigeria, was isolated and treated by Nigerian health workers before being medically evacuated to Switzerland on October 26 for further treatment after her condition stabilised. Her husband, who was identified as a close contact, was also evacuated. Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said Nigeria had no confirmed Ebola cases. However, the WHO clarified that the development did not mean Nigeria had been declared Ebola-free, explaining that health authorities were still monitoring people who had contact with the patient. The organisation said Nigeria must complete the required 42-day monitoring period before an official Ebola-free declaration could be made. In its October 29 situation report, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control (NCDC) said 62 contacts linked to the index case had been identified and were being monitored. The agency added that no new contacts or symptomatic contacts had been identified in the preceding 24 hours. The continued spread of the disease has heightened concerns about cross-border transmission and the capacity of African countries to contain infectious diseases amid increased movement of people across the continent. The post Ebola outbreak not under control in Africa, CDC warns appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Konongo, Juansa chiefs back revocation of Northern Ashanti Mines license
items.description: Traditional authorities in Konongo and Juansa have backed the revocation of the mining license of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited in its catchment. They cite poor performance, environmental degradation and neglect of responsibilities towards local communities. This comes after the Minerals Commission terminated the company’s mineral rights following allegations that portions of the concession were given to illegal miners. Staff have since been asked to vacate the concession as the mine is non-operational. Chief of Konongo, Nana Dr. Awuah Abedimsa II, supports the Commission. “Minerals Commission is the statutory body responsible for mining and they have performance indicators which they use in measuring the performance of all Mining Companies. So the action taken by the minerals commission on behalf of the Konongo mine, I agree with it,” he said. He added that “the Northern Ashanti Mines in my opinion didn’t have the resources to mine the deposits and it has given rise to the environmental degradation that we fought and continue to fight against.” He wants the mine given to credible investors. Chief of Juansa, Nana Tweneboah Kodua Bempah, also backs a reset. “The illegal miners have destroyed some water bodies in the area. Our community largely depend on farming and whoever mines there should do it responsibly. We need people who will mine responsibly so we can protect our river bodies,” he said. Government intervention The lease was granted to Owere Mines in January 2010 covering 595 cadastral blocks. Under Section 24 of Act 703, it was bound to pay Annual Mineral Right fees, which it failed to do so. The Minerals Commission says it exercised persistent forbearance issuing a Notice to Remedy Breach in May 2020 when arrears exceeded US$4 million. The company, transitioning to BCM Investments, proposed payment in four tranches which it failed to meet its own plan. The Commission issued successive notices between 2020 and 2025. Debt rose from US$5.5 million in October 2022 to US$6.1 million in December 2022, and to US$8.33 million for mining leases plus US$49,928 for prospecting licences by April 2025. The company failed to make payments. On April 7, 2026, the Commission deemed the breach flagrant and deliberate and requested the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources to terminate. The Minister approved and the rights were terminated. The Commission rejects claims that the US$8 million figure is wrong and disputes the company’s claim of paying US$1 million. Its records show only US$300,000 paid. “For a company that claims to have spent US$200,000,000 on the mine, what prevented it from paying the US$8,000,000 owed to the people of Ghana?” it queried. Under Section 70 of Act 703, terminated rights revert to the State. The State will secure the assets and pursue all outstanding liabilities. “A mineral right is not a gift, and it is not an inheritance! It is a privilege conferred by the State on terms, and those terms must be honoured,” the Commission said, insisting it acted lawfully and with due process. The military remains stationed at the facility as the government is expected to announce next steps.

items.title: La Mauritanie entreprend la mise en place d’une nouvelle politique à l’endroit de sa diaspora
items.description: Le ministre mauritanien des Affaires étrangères, Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug, a déclaré vendredi que le gouvernement s’employait à élaborer une politique nationale plus efficace à l'égard des Mauritaniens résidant à l'étranger, fondée sur des consultations directes avec les communautés et sur le suivi de leurs besoins et des défis auxquels elles sont confrontées dans leurs pays de résidence. Dans un discours prononcé lors de l’inauguration du Forum des communautés mauritaniennes à l’étranger, Ould Merzoug a précisé que ces consultations avaient donné lieu à des rencontres avec des représentants des communautés dans 23 pays et avaient porté sur les problèmes liés aux services consulaires, à l’authentification des actes, à l’état civil, au séjour, à l’intégration ainsi qu’à la protection sociale et juridique, sans oublier l’éducation, la préservation de l’identité et l’organisation des communautés. Le ministre a ajouté que le ministère avait classé les résultats de ces consultations et les avait transformés en axes de discussion et d’action, avec la participation de secteurs gouvernementaux, d’institutions nationales, du Parlement, du secteur privé, de la société civile et d’experts, dans le but de définir les priorités et de rechercher des solutions concrètes. Le ministre a souligné que ces consultations ont mis en évidence le potentiel économique, scientifique et professionnel des communautés, qui peut être mis à profit pour soutenir le développement national. Il a précisé que le forum permet de faciliter les échanges entre les talents et les investisseurs issus de la communauté, les institutions et les acteurs économiques, et d’étudier la transformation des initiatives en partenariats et en projets. Les travaux du forum, qui s’étendent sur trois jours, portent sur le développement et la numérisation des services consulaires, le renforcement de la protection sociale et juridique, la mobilisation des compétences et le transfert de savoir-faire, la promotion de l’investissement et de l’entrepreneuriat, ainsi que le rôle des transferts de fonds des expatriés dans le développement, sans oublier les questions liées à l’éducation, à la culture et à l’identité nationale. Ould Merzoug a souligné que le gouvernement espère que les travaux du forum déboucheront sur des recommandations précises et applicables, comprenant des priorités claires et des mécanismes de suivi, en vue de l’élaboration d’une politique nationale répondant aux spécificités de la Mauritanie et à la situation de ses communautés à l’étranger.
